```{r setup}
.libPaths(c(getwd(),.libPaths()))

.pkg_lib <- file.path(getwd(), "R_runtime_libs")
dir.create(.pkg_lib, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
.libPaths(c(.pkg_lib, .libPaths()))

.pkg_repos <- local({
  r <- getOption("repos")
  r <- r[!is.na(r) & nzchar(r) & r != "@CRAN@"]
  if (length(r) == 0) c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  else unique(c(r, CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
})

install_if_missing <- function(pkg, required = TRUE) {
  if (requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) return(invisible(TRUE))
  try(install.packages(pkg, repos = .pkg_repos, quiet = TRUE, lib = .pkg_lib),
      silent = TRUE)
  ok <- requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)
  if (!ok && isTRUE(required)) {
    stop(sprintf(paste0(
      "Required R package '%s' is missing and could not be installed.\n",
      "  repos tried : %s\n",
      "  lib target  : %s\n",
      "This host has no working route to a package repository. Either bake '%s'\n",
      "into the SV_REPORT_INDEX container image (preferred - see the TODO below),\n",
      "or export http_proxy/https_proxy for the task so the runtime install works."),
      pkg, paste(.pkg_repos, collapse = ", "), .pkg_lib, pkg), call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(ok)
}
install_if_missing("DT")
install_if_missing("plotly")

# Runtime Bioconductor install — used for the optional EnsDb breakend
# annotation block. Rocker/verse ships a P3M repos config so BiocManager
# prefers binaries when available, keeping cold install closer to seconds
# than compile-from-source minutes. Wrapped in tryCatch so a repo miss or
# transient network hiccup falls back to the downstream `requireNamespace`
# gate rather than killing the whole render.
# TODO: bake ensembldb + plyranges into a custom SV_REPORT_INDEX container
# image so this runtime install can be removed.
install_bioc_if_missing <- function(pkg) {
  if (requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) return(invisible(TRUE))
  tryCatch({
    if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
      install.packages("BiocManager", repos = .pkg_repos,
                       quiet = TRUE, lib = .pkg_lib)
    }
    BiocManager::install(pkg, update = FALSE, ask = FALSE, quiet = TRUE,
                         lib = .pkg_lib)
    invisible(TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Optional Bioc install skipped for '", pkg, "': ",
            conditionMessage(e))
    invisible(FALSE)
  })
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(DT)
  library(plotly)
})

#  Reusable predicates / normalizers (tidyverse-patterns) 
# True iff x has real annotation content (handles NA, "", ".", "NA", "()").
is_meaningful <- function(x) {
  !is.na(x) & !(x %in% c("", ".", "NA", "()"))
}

# Strip InfoTuple-style "(...)" / quote decoration from a vembrane TSV cell and
# return the first element as a clean string. Splits on EITHER `,` or `;`. The `,` handles raw vembrane InfoTuple input like "('5', 'full=5')" while `;` handles the output like "5; full=5; full=5"
# scalar_first applied value returns the entire joined string and downstream as.integer() / factor() match returns NA.
scalar_first <- function(x) {
  cleaned <- str_replace_all(as.character(x), "[()'\"\\s]", "")
  str_split_fixed(cleaned, "[,;]", 2)[, 1]
}

# Cast ACMG_class to an ordered factor for plot ordering and color mapping.
# NA-like inputs (R-NA, empty string, ".", literal "NA") are normalized to the
# explicit "NA" factor level so plots can render them as grey via the
# acmg_palette mapping below (true-NA factor values would render transparent
# under scale_fill_viridis_d).
acmg_factor <- function(x) {
  s <- scalar_first(x)
  s[is.na(s) | s %in% c("", ".", "NA")] <- "NA"
  factor(s, levels = c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "NA"))
}

# Strict ACMG cleaner for the cohort TSV: returns integer 1-5 or NA_integer_.
# Coerces 0 (AnnotSV "unclassified") and any non-1-5 value to NA. Designed to
# overwrite the raw ACMG_class column in the cohort TSV — NOT a replacement
# for acmg_factor(), which intentionally keeps "0" / "NA" as factor levels
# for plot color mapping.
acmg_clean <- function(x) {
  s <- scalar_first(x)
  n <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(s))
  ifelse(is.na(n) | n < 1L | n > 5L, NA_integer_, n)
}

# Color palette: viridis "rocket" ramp for ACMG classes 0–5, grey for "NA".
# Used by Plot 2 (ACMG class stacked bars) via scale_fill_manual so the
# NA category renders as grey instead of transparent.
acmg_palette <- c(
  setNames(viridisLite::rocket(6, direction = -1, end = 0.85),
           c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5")),
  "NA" = "grey70"
)

#  BND partner-chromosome validation for ST17 hits 
# AnnotSV's user-BED overlap test only checks one breakpoint of a BND
# record against the BED interval.
#
# Current ST17 BED `name` column format (post gene-annotation update):
#   "chrA:posA-chrB:posB_(geneA::geneB)"                (single hit)
#   "hit1|hit2|hit3|..."                                (multi-hit, '|'-sep)
#

# Strip a leading "chr" (any case) so "chr21", "Chr21", "21" all compare equal.
normalize_chrom <- function(s) {
  sub("^chr", "", as.character(s), ignore.case = TRUE)
}

# Strip InfoTuple wrapping `('val',)` -> `val`. Pass-through for already-clean strings.
strip_infotuple <- function(s) {
  s <- as.character(s)
  s <- sub("^\\(['\"]", "", s)
  s <- sub("['\"],?\\s*\\)$", "", s)
  s
}

# Clean vembrane's TSV-encoded ClinVar_SV_CLNSIG cell into a semicolon-joined
# list of unique significance labels. VEP's --custom for the ClinVar SV VCF emits per-overlap CLNSIG values wrapped in double quotes and joined with "&", e.g. `"Pathogenic"&"Pathogenic"&"Likely%20pathogenic"&"Benign"`. 
clean_clinvar_clnsig <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return("")
  s <- str_replace_all(as.character(x), '"', '')
  parts <- str_split(s, "&")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts)]
  paste(unique(parts), collapse = "; ")
}

# Vectorized breakpoint formatter for the DT `breakpoint` column.
#
# Intra-chromosomal SVs / CNAs (DEL, DUP, INV, INS, CNV):
#   "chr21:100000-110000"   (if END > POS)
#   "chr21:100000"          (if END == POS or END missing)
#
# Interchromosomal BNDs (parses partner from ALT bracket notation, all
# four VCF spec forms: t[p[ , [p[t , t]p] , ]p]t):
#   "chr21:100000|chr5:300000"
#
# BND with unparseable ALT falls back to "chr21:100000".
#
# Fully vectorized via `str_match` on the ALT column (no rowwise). The
# `chr` prefix is added when absent (raw CHROM in the merged VCF is bare
# "21" while ALT partner uses "chr21" — normalize both sides for consistent
# display).
compute_breakpoint <- function(chrom, pos, end, alt, svtype) {
  chrom  <- as.character(chrom)
  pos    <- as.character(pos)
  end    <- as.character(end)
  alt    <- as.character(alt)
  svtype <- as.character(svtype)

  prefix_chr <- function(c) ifelse(is.na(c) | !nzchar(c) | startsWith(c, "chr"),
                                   c, paste0("chr", c))

  chrom <- prefix_chr(chrom)

  # BND if SVTYPE says so OR if ALT has bracket notation
  is_bnd <- (svtype == "BND") | grepl("[\\[\\]]", alt)

  # Vectorized partner parse from bracket notation
  m <- str_match(alt, "[\\[\\]]([^:\\[\\]]+):([0-9]+)[\\[\\]]")
  p_chr <- prefix_chr(m[, 2])
  p_pos <- m[, 3]
  partner_ok <- !is.na(p_chr) & !is.na(p_pos)

  # Intra-chromosomal display: "chr:pos-end" or "chr:pos" when end is
  # missing / equals pos (typical for INS)
  end_valid <- !is.na(end) & nzchar(end) & end != "." & end != pos
  intra <- ifelse(end_valid,
                  paste0(chrom, ":", pos, "-", end),
                  paste0(chrom, ":", pos))

  ifelse(
    is_bnd & partner_ok,
    paste0(chrom, ":", pos, "|", p_chr, ":", p_pos),
    intra
  )
}

# Round a comma-joined hVAF cell to 2 decimal places.
# Input:  "0.800000011920929,0.0,0.0"  (HP1, HP2, unphased triple)
# Output: "0.80,0.00,0.00"
# Preserves the 3-value tuple shape; missing/empty inputs pass through.
format_hvaf <- function(x, digits = 2L) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return("")
  parts <- str_split(as.character(x), ",")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  parts <- vapply(parts, function(v) {
    n <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v))
    if (is.na(n)) v else formatC(n, format = "f", digits = digits)
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  paste(parts, collapse = ",")
}

# check if a bnd is intra or interchromosomal 
chk_intra_bnd <- function(breakpoint){
  be <- str_split_1(breakpoint, pattern = "\\|") |>  gsub(pattern = "(.+):[0-9]+", replacement = "\\1", x = _)
  if(length(be) == 2){
    intrachrom <- be[1] == be[2]
  } else {
    intrachrom <- TRUE
  }
  return(intrachrom)
}

# Summarize an AnnotSV P_*_source (P_gain_source / P_loss_source /
# P_ins_source) cell into a compact "first-3 + count" per category form.
#
# Input format: the raw INFO field is Number=. String — one entry per
# overlapping annotated interval, each entry pipe-separated hits with the
# source prefix. vembrane's chr(44).join(InfoTuple) delivers the whole cell
# as ONE string with commas between entries and pipes within entries, e.g.:
#   "dbVar:nssv1|dbVar:nssv2|morbid:APP|morbid:BACH1,.,.,dbVar:nssv2|morbid:APP,."
#
# Output form (per cell):
#   "dbVar[3/12]: nssv1|nssv2|nssv3; morbid[3/8]: APP|BACH1|JAM2;
#    CLN[2]: 3779864|552391; HI3[1]: DYRK1A"
# For dbVar and morbid we show first-3 hits + total (unique) count. For
# CLN and HI3 we show first-3 hits + count too. Bare `nssv*` (no prefix)
# is categorized as dbVar per AnnotSV convention. Empty / all-"." input
# returns "".
summarize_p_source <- function(x, top_n = 3L) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return("")
  # Explode across commas (Number=. entries) and pipes (per-hit)
  parts <- str_split(as.character(x), "[,|]")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts) & parts != "."]
  if (length(parts) == 0) return("")
  # Categorize
  cat_of <- function(h) {
    if (startsWith(h, "dbVar:") || startsWith(h, "nssv")) return("dbVar")
    if (startsWith(h, "morbid:")) return("morbid")
    if (startsWith(h, "CLN:"))    return("CLN")
    if (startsWith(h, "HI3:"))    return("HI3")
    if (startsWith(h, "TS3:"))    return("TS3")
    "other"
  }
  # Strip prefix for display
  strip_prefix <- function(h) sub("^[A-Za-z0-9]+:", "", h)

  cats  <- vapply(parts, cat_of, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  bags  <- split(parts, cats)
  order_shown <- c("dbVar", "morbid", "CLN", "HI3", "TS3", "other")
  order_shown <- order_shown[order_shown %in% names(bags)]

  fmt_one <- function(cat) {
    uniq <- unique(bags[[cat]])
    shown <- head(vapply(uniq, strip_prefix, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE), top_n)
    sprintf("%s[%d/%d]: %s", cat, length(shown), length(uniq),
            paste(shown, collapse = "|"))
  }
  paste(vapply(order_shown, fmt_one, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
        collapse = "; ")
}

# Clean AnnotSV's `full,split,split,...` padding pattern. When an AnnotSV
# TSV row is converted to VCF INFO, the full-mode value is at index 0 and
# the split-mode entries follow at positions 1..N. Fields that vary per
# split (Gene_name, Location, etc.) get real values; fields that only exist
# in full mode get "." for every split → strings like "value,.,.,.,.".
# Split on ",", drop "." and empty tokens, rejoin with ",". Idempotent —
# a cell that never had padding (already clean) round-trips unchanged.
clean_annot_padding <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return("")
  parts <- str_split(as.character(x), ",")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts) & parts != "."]
  paste(parts, collapse = ",")
}

# Split on both `,` and `|`, drop empties / ".", return unique tokens in
# first-seen order joined with a single delimiter. Used for AnnotSV fields
# where full-mode emits a `|`-joined multi-value list and split-mode repeats
# the same values comma-appended (Gene_name, CytoBand, Location).
dedup_annot_multi <- function(x, sep = "; ") {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return("")
  parts <- str_split(as.character(x), "[,|]\\s*")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts) & parts != "."]
  if (length(parts) == 0) return("")
  paste(unique(parts), collapse = sep)
}

# Collapse a multi-cytoband CytoBand string to its encompassing range.
# For large CNAs / SVs, AnnotSV emits both a "full" annotation with the
# encompassing range (e.g. `q23.31-q26.3`) and per-split-mode annotations
# for every sub-band inside (`q23.31`, `q23.32`, `q23.32-q23.33`, …). After
# `dedup_annot_multi()` runs, the CytoBand cell looks like:
#     q23.31-q26.3; q23.31; q23.32; q23.32-q23.33; q23.33; q24.1; ...
# which is technically deduplicated (every distinct sub-range is unique)
# but useless in the DT display. Collapse to a single `<min>-<max>` range
# by parsing every position token (splitting ranges at `-`), sorting by
# (arm, major, sub) ascending, and rebuilding the outermost interval.
#
# Input examples → outputs:
#   "q23.31"                                    → "q23.31"
#   "q23.31; q23.32"                            → "q23.31-q23.32"
#   "q23.31-q26.3; q23.31; ...; q26.3"          → "q23.31-q26.3"
#   "p13.2; p13.1"                              → "p13.1-p13.2"   (p arm order)
#   ""  / "." / NA                              → ""
#
# p-arm bands are sorted with the LARGER major number distal (further from
# centromere) — i.e. p13 comes before p11 when reading toward the centromere.
# For range endpoints we still take alphanumeric min-max of the numeric part
# on each arm; the display convention is "smaller number - larger number"
# per arm, matching how AnnotSV writes its own full-mode ranges.
collapse_cytoband_range <- function(cytoband_str) {
  if (is.na(cytoband_str) || !nzchar(cytoband_str) || cytoband_str == ".") return("")
  parts <- str_split(as.character(cytoband_str), "[;,|]\\s*")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  parts <- parts[nzchar(parts) & parts != "."]
  if (length(parts) == 0) return("")

  # Break any pre-existing ranges (e.g. "q23.31-q26.3") into their two
  # endpoint tokens so we sort on a flat vector of atomic positions.
  positions <- unlist(lapply(parts, function(p) {
    if (grepl("-", p, fixed = TRUE)) str_split(p, "-")[[1]] else p
  }))
  positions <- unique(positions[nzchar(positions)])
  if (length(positions) == 0) return("")
  if (length(positions) == 1) return(positions[1])

  # Sort into chromosomal (linear) order — p-telomere → centromere → q-telomere.
  # On the p arm, HIGHER band numbers are DISTAL (closer to telomere, i.e. lower
  # linear position): p13.3 < p13.2 < p13.1 in chromosomal position; AnnotSV
  # writes p-arm ranges telomere-to-centromere → descending numeric.
  # On the q arm, HIGHER band numbers are DISTAL (further from centromere, i.e.
  # higher linear position): q11.1 < q11.2 < q13.3 in chromosomal position;
  # AnnotSV writes q-arm ranges centromere-to-telomere → ascending numeric.
  # Sub-band digit strings compare LEXICOGRAPHICALLY (not numerically) since
  # they're nested labels: q26.1 contains q26.11 / q26.12 / q26.13, and q26.2
  # comes AFTER q26.13. Lex "13" < "3" because '1' < '3' — correct order.
  parse_key <- function(p) {
    m <- regmatches(p, regexec("^([pq])(\\d+)(?:\\.(\\d+))?$", p))[[1]]
    if (length(m) < 3 || !nzchar(m[2])) return(list(arm=3L, major=999L, sub="~"))
    arm_rank <- if (m[2] == "p") 1L else 2L
    major <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(m[3])) %||% 999L
    sub   <- if (length(m) >= 4 && nzchar(m[4])) m[4] else ""
    list(arm = arm_rank, major = major, sub = sub)
  }
  keys <- lapply(positions, parse_key)
  arms   <- vapply(keys, `[[`, integer(1),   "arm")
  majors <- vapply(keys, `[[`, integer(1),   "major")
  subs   <- vapply(keys, `[[`, character(1), "sub")

  # Sort each arm independently, then concat p-then-q to get chromosomal order.
  #   p arm: sort ascending (major, sub) then REVERSE — high band numbers first
  #          (most telomeric on p side)
  #   q arm: sort ascending (major, sub) directly
  is_p <- arms == 1L
  is_q <- arms == 2L
  is_x <- arms == 3L  # unrecognized tokens sink to the end
  p_ord <- rev(order(majors[is_p], subs[is_p]))
  q_ord <- order(majors[is_q], subs[is_q])
  x_ord <- order(subs[is_x])
  sorted <- c(positions[is_p][p_ord],
              positions[is_q][q_ord],
              positions[is_x][x_ord])
  min_p <- sorted[1]
  max_p <- sorted[length(sorted)]
  if (min_p == max_p) return(min_p)
  paste0(min_p, "-", max_p)
}

# Parse a CIViC INFO annotation cell into a fixed set of interpretive columns.
# The CIViC VCF annotation loaded via `bcftools annotate` uses a VEP-style
# 40-field pipe-delimited entry; a record with N CIViC assertions carries N
# such entries joined by ",". This helper extracts the seven columns
# requested for downstream clinical review, deduplicates across per-record
# entries (multi-therapy / multi-evidence records collapse cleanly), and
# returns a named list of atomic character scalars suitable for
# `dplyr::mutate(...)` splatting. Field indices are fixed by the CIViC
# header (see the CIVIC INFO Description in the annotate_civic_snv VCF):
#   0 Allele        1 Consequence   2 SYMBOL          9 CIViC Variant ID
#  11 CIViC Variant URL             24 CIViC Entity Variant Origin
#  29 CIViC Entity Therapies        34 CIViC Assertion ACMG Codes
parse_civic_field <- function(civic_str) {
  empty <- list(
    CIViC_Consequence           = NA_character_,
    CIViC_SYMBOL                = NA_character_,
    CIViC_Variant_ID            = NA_character_,
    CIViC_Variant_URL           = NA_character_,
    CIViC_Entity_Variant_Origin = NA_character_,
    CIViC_Entity_Therapies      = NA_character_,
    CIViC_Assertion_ACMG_Codes  = NA_character_
  )
  s <- as.character(civic_str)
  if (is.na(s) || !nzchar(s) || s %in% c("NA", ".")) return(empty)

  hits <- str_split(s, ",")[[1]]
  fields_list <- lapply(hits, function(h) {
    v <- str_split(h, "\\|")[[1]]
    length(v) <- 40L
    v
  })

  # 0-indexed in the CIViC header; +1 for R.
  extract_col <- function(idx0) {
    vals <- vapply(fields_list, function(v) {
      x <- v[idx0 + 1L]
      if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) NA_character_ else x
    }, character(1))
    vals <- unique(vals[!is.na(vals)])
    if (length(vals) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(vals, collapse = ";")
  }

  list(
    CIViC_Consequence           = extract_col(1L),
    CIViC_SYMBOL                = extract_col(2L),
    CIViC_Variant_ID            = extract_col(9L),
    CIViC_Variant_URL           = extract_col(11L),
    CIViC_Entity_Variant_Origin = extract_col(24L),
    CIViC_Entity_Therapies      = extract_col(29L),
    CIViC_Assertion_ACMG_Codes  = extract_col(34L)
  )
}


# Vectorized full clean of vembrane InfoTuple representations across a column.
clean_tuple <- function(x) {
  s <- as.character(x)
  out <- s
  hit <- !is.na(s) & grepl("^\\(.*\\)$", s)
  if (any(hit)) {
    out[hit] <- vapply(s[hit], function(t) {
      # Strip outer parens (and trailing comma for single-element tuples)
      inner <- sub("^\\(", "", sub(",?\\s*\\)$", "", t))
      # Capture all single- or double-quoted elements
      m <- str_match_all(inner, "'([^']*)'|\"([^\"]*)\"")[[1]]
      if (nrow(m) == 0) return(inner)
      vals <- ifelse(is.na(m[, 2]), m[, 3], m[, 2])
      paste(vals, collapse = "; ")
    }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Load a one-gene-per-line file into a character vector for Candidate_genes
# Returns an empty vector if the params$candidate_genes path is missing or empty.
load_candidate_gene_set <- function() {
  fp <- params$candidate_genes
  if (is.null(fp) || !nzchar(fp) || !file.exists(fp)) return(character(0))
  lines <- readLines(fp, warn = FALSE)
  trimmed <- str_trim(lines)
  trimmed[nzchar(trimmed) & !startsWith(trimmed, "#")]
}

# Union candidate-gene detection across Gene_name (SV interval overlap) +
# Closest_left / Closest_right (nearest flanking gene). Intergenic BND
# breakpoints have empty Gene_name but often carry a driver gene as the
# closest-flanking annotation — critical for T-ALL where BND-mediated fusion
# partners land in intergenic regions. Returns a "; "-joined string of unique
# candidate-gene hits across the three columns, in first-seen order.
compute_candidate_genes <- function(gene_name, closest_left, closest_right,
                                    candidate_set) {
  if (length(candidate_set) == 0) return("")
  raw <- c(gene_name, closest_left, closest_right)
  raw <- raw[!is.na(raw) & nzchar(raw)]
  if (length(raw) == 0) return("")
  parts <- unlist(lapply(raw, function(s) str_trim(str_split(s, "[|;]\\s*")[[1]])))
  hits  <- unique(parts[parts %in% candidate_set])
  paste(hits, collapse = "; ")
}

# Summarize a Gene_name list for display: if the underlying gene count
# exceeds `cap`, truncate to the first `cap` genes and append " (n=<count>
# genes)"; otherwise return the raw joined string unchanged. `count` should
# be the AnnotSV Gene_count column value (authoritative — includes genes
# that may have been de-duplicated in the display string). Falls back to
# counting the delimiter-split length when count is NA / empty.
summarize_gene_list <- function(gene_str, count = NA_integer_, cap = 20L) {
  if (is.na(gene_str) || !nzchar(gene_str)) return("")
  genes <- str_split(gene_str, "[|;]\\s*")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  genes <- genes[nzchar(genes)]
  n_parsed <- length(genes)
  n_auth <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(count))
  n_show <- if (!is.na(n_auth) && n_auth > 0) n_auth else n_parsed
  if (n_show > cap) {
    paste0(paste(head(genes, cap), collapse = "; "),
           "; ... (n=", n_show, " genes)")
  } else {
    paste(genes, collapse = "; ")
  }
}

# Parse an ST17 score cell (semicolon- or comma-joined multi-hit) and return
# the maximum integer score. Falls back to 0 for empty / non-numeric input.
# Used as the tier-1 tie-breaker in driver_tier ranking (recurrence-count
# proxy: highest ST17 score = most recurrent T-ALL SV).
parse_st17_max_score <- function(score_str) {
  if (is.na(score_str) || !nzchar(score_str)) return(0L)
  toks <- str_split(score_str, "[,;|]\\s*")[[1]] |> str_trim()
  vals <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(toks))
  vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
  if (length(vals) == 0) 0L else max(vals)
}

# Pair-split an ST17 (name, score) cell together so downstream ordering is
# stable and interpretable. AnnotSV emits multi-hit ST17 cells with two
# different join-levels: the name field can hold multiple gene-pair
# alternatives inside a single BED row's `_(GENE_A|_GENE_B::GENE_C|_GENE_D)`
# construct AND multiple BED rows joined by `|`; the score field carries one
# score per BED row joined by `|`. That mismatch is why a length-5 name and
# length-2 score can appear in the same record. This function:
#   1. Splits name via `split_pipe_outside_parens` (respects `_(...|...)`).
#   2. Splits score by `|` at outer level.
#   3. Drops empty/"." tokens (residual `clean_annot_padding` artefacts).
#   4. Pairs by index — if scores shorter than names (AnnotSV pipe-mismatch),
#      the LAST score is repeated to fill (a per-BED-row score naturally
#      applies to every gene-pair variant inside that BED row's name field).
#   5. De-duplicates by name (keeps highest-score occurrence).
#   6. Orders by score desc (NA last) and truncates to `top_n` hits.
# Returns a named list of two `|`-joined strings so downstream code can
# either display them jointly (`ST17_hit`) or feed the score string into
# `parse_st17_max_score` for tier tie-breaking.
parse_st17_pair <- function(name_str, score_str, top_n = 3L) {
  empty_result <- list(names = "", scores = "")
  if (is.na(name_str) || !nzchar(name_str) || name_str == ".") return(empty_result)

  names_v <- split_pipe_outside_parens(as.character(name_str))
  names_v <- names_v[nzchar(names_v) & names_v != "."]
  if (length(names_v) == 0) return(empty_result)

  scores_num <- if (is.na(score_str) || !nzchar(score_str) || score_str == ".") {
    integer(0)
  } else {
    toks <- str_split(as.character(score_str), "\\|")[[1]] |> str_trim()
    toks <- toks[nzchar(toks) & toks != "."]
    suppressWarnings(as.integer(toks))
  }
  scores_num <- scores_num[!is.na(scores_num)]

  n_names  <- length(names_v)
  n_scores <- length(scores_num)
  if (n_scores == 0) {
    paired <- rep(NA_integer_, n_names)
  } else if (n_scores >= n_names) {
    paired <- scores_num[seq_len(n_names)]
  } else {
    paired <- c(scores_num, rep(scores_num[n_scores], n_names - n_scores))
  }

  ord <- order(paired, decreasing = TRUE, na.last = TRUE)
  names_v <- names_v[ord]
  paired  <- paired[ord]

  keep <- !duplicated(names_v)
  names_v <- names_v[keep]
  paired  <- paired[keep]

  n_take <- min(as.integer(top_n), length(names_v))
  list(
    names  = paste(names_v[seq_len(n_take)], collapse = "|"),
    scores = paste(ifelse(is.na(paired[seq_len(n_take)]), "",
                          as.character(paired[seq_len(n_take)])),
                   collapse = "|")
  )
}

# Assign a T-ALL driver-priority tier per pass2 record:
#   Tier 1 = any SVTYPE-matched name_ST17_* hit (empirical T-ALL recurrence)
#   Tier 2 = no ST17 hit, but ≥1 Candidate_genes match (literature prior)
#   Tier 3 = neither (still passed pass2 by other evidence — P_gain_source,
#                     RE_gene, ACMG 3-5, or ClinVar pathogenic)
# Tie-breaker `tier_score` (higher = better):
#   T1: max integer score across SVTYPE-matched score_ST17_* — proxies
#       T-ALL cohort recurrence
#   T2: number of overlapping candidate genes — more hits = broader impact
#   T3: AnnotSV_ranking_score — falls back to AnnotSV's own ranking
# Returns a tibble with columns `driver_tier` (integer 1-3) and
# `tier_score` (numeric).
assign_driver_tier <- function(st17_name, st17_score, candidate_genes,
                                annotsv_ranking_score) {
  has_st17 <- !is.na(st17_name) & nzchar(st17_name)
  has_cand <- !is.na(candidate_genes) & nzchar(candidate_genes)
  tier <- ifelse(has_st17, 1L,
                 ifelse(has_cand, 2L, 3L))
  cand_n <- vapply(candidate_genes, function(s) {
    if (is.na(s) || !nzchar(s)) return(0L)
    length(str_split(s, ";\\s*")[[1]])
  }, integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  st17_max <- vapply(st17_score, parse_st17_max_score,
                     integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  ann_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(annotsv_ranking_score))
  ann_num[is.na(ann_num)] <- 0
  score <- ifelse(tier == 1L, as.numeric(st17_max),
                  ifelse(tier == 2L, as.numeric(cand_n), ann_num))
  tibble::tibble(driver_tier = tier, tier_score = score)
}

# CNA driver-priority tier 
# BED CNV 
#   Tier 1 = any SVTYPE-matched name_ST19_* hit 
#            match GAIN records -> AMP+GAIN cols, LOSS records -> DEL+LOSS)
#   Tier 2 = no ST19 hit, but ≥1 Candidate_genes match
#   Tier 3 = neither (P_gain_source, ACMG 3-5, etc.)
# Tie-breaker `tier_score`:
#   T1: max score across the 4 score_ST19_* columns
#   T2: number of overlapping candidate genes
#   T3: AnnotSV_ranking_score
assign_driver_tier_cna <- function(st19_amp_name, st19_del_name,
                                    st19_gain_name, st19_loss_name,
                                    st19_amp_score, st19_del_score,
                                    st19_gain_score, st19_loss_score,
                                    candidate_genes, annotsv_ranking_score) {
  st19_names <- list(st19_amp_name, st19_del_name, st19_gain_name, st19_loss_name)
  st19_scores <- list(st19_amp_score, st19_del_score, st19_gain_score, st19_loss_score)

  has_st19 <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(st19_names, function(v) !is.na(v) & nzchar(v)))
  has_cand <- !is.na(candidate_genes) & nzchar(candidate_genes)
  tier <- ifelse(has_st19, 1L,
                 ifelse(has_cand, 2L, 3L))

  cand_n <- vapply(candidate_genes, function(s) {
    if (is.na(s) || !nzchar(s)) return(0L)
    length(str_split(s, ";\\s*")[[1]])
  }, integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)

  st19_max <- pmax(
    vapply(st19_amp_score,  parse_st17_max_score, integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
    vapply(st19_del_score,  parse_st17_max_score, integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
    vapply(st19_gain_score, parse_st17_max_score, integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
    vapply(st19_loss_score, parse_st17_max_score, integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  ann_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(annotsv_ranking_score))
  ann_num[is.na(ann_num)] <- 0
  score <- ifelse(tier == 1L, as.numeric(st19_max),
                  ifelse(tier == 2L, as.numeric(cand_n), ann_num))
  tibble::tibble(driver_tier = tier, tier_score = score)
}

# SNV driver-priority tier 
# candidate-gene evidence.
#   Tier 1 = ONC = "Oncogenic" OR "Likely_oncogenic" AND SYMBOL in candidate panel
#   Tier 2 = ClinVar pathogenic/likely_pathogenic OR candidate-gene member
#   Tier 3 = neither ( SIFT deleterious / PolyPhen damaging predictions) 
# Tie-breaker `tier_score` = max(CLAIRSTO_VAF, DEEPSOMATIC_VAF) — somatic. ties broken by higher confidence in the somatic call.
assign_driver_tier_snv <- function(onc, clnsig, candidate_genes,
                                    clairsto_vaf, deepsomatic_vaf) {
  onc_str    <- as.character(onc)
  clnsig_str <- as.character(clnsig)
  cand_str   <- as.character(candidate_genes)

  # ONC substring: "Oncogenic" and "Likely_oncogenic"
  # ClinVar substring: "Pathogenic", "Likely_pathogenic", "Pathogenic_low_penetrance"
  has_onc  <- !is.na(onc_str) &
              grepl("ncogenic", onc_str, ignore.case = TRUE)
  has_cln  <- !is.na(clnsig_str) &
              grepl("athogenic", clnsig_str, ignore.case = TRUE)
  has_cand <- !is.na(cand_str) & nzchar(cand_str)

  tier <- ifelse(has_onc & has_cand, 1L,
                 ifelse(has_cln | has_cand, 2L, 3L))

  vaf <- pmax(
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(clairsto_vaf)),
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(deepsomatic_vaf)),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  vaf[is.na(vaf) | is.infinite(vaf)] <- 0
  tibble::tibble(driver_tier = tier, tier_score = vaf)
}

# Split on '|' but only at paren depth 0 — the ST17 hit format embeds gene
# annotations like `_(RUNX1|_TLX3::TLX3|_RUNX1)` where the inner '|' is
# part of one hit, not a hit-separator. `str_split` doesn't natively
# respect bracket nesting; this manual scanner does.
split_pipe_outside_parens <- function(s) {
  if (length(s) == 0 || is.na(s) || s == "") return(character(0))
  chars <- strsplit(s, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  depth <- 0L
  parts <- character(0)
  current <- ""
  for (ch in chars) {
    if (ch == "(") { depth <- depth + 1L; current <- paste0(current, ch) }
    else if (ch == ")") { depth <- max(depth - 1L, 0L); current <- paste0(current, ch) }
    else if (ch == "|" && depth == 0L) {
      parts <- c(parts, current); current <- ""
    } else {
      current <- paste0(current, ch)
    }
  }
  c(parts, current)
}

# Parse the partner-side breakpoint from a Severus/SAVANA BND ALT.
# Handles all four VCF spec bracket forms: t[p[ , [p[t , t]p] , ]p]t.
parse_bnd_partner <- function(alt) {
  if (is.na(alt) || alt == "") return(list(chrom = NA_character_, pos = NA_real_))
  m <- str_match(alt, "[\\[\\]]([^:\\[\\]]+):([0-9]+)[\\[\\]]")
  if (is.na(m[1, 2])) return(list(chrom = NA_character_, pos = NA_real_))
  list(chrom = normalize_chrom(m[1, 2]), pos = as.numeric(m[1, 3]))
}

# Test whether a sample's two breakpoints overlap a reference pair within
# `tol` bp, trying both pair orderings (BND pairs are unordered).
bnd_pair_matches <- function(s_chrom_a, s_pos_a, s_chrom_b, s_pos_b,
                              r_chrom_a, r_pos_a, r_chrom_b, r_pos_b,
                              tol = 10000) {
  s_a <- normalize_chrom(s_chrom_a); s_b <- normalize_chrom(s_chrom_b)
  r_a <- normalize_chrom(r_chrom_a); r_b <- normalize_chrom(r_chrom_b)
  direct  <- (s_a == r_a && abs(s_pos_a - r_pos_a) <= tol &&
              s_b == r_b && abs(s_pos_b - r_pos_b) <= tol)
  swapped <- (s_a == r_b && abs(s_pos_a - r_pos_b) <= tol &&
              s_b == r_a && abs(s_pos_b - r_pos_a) <= tol)
  isTRUE(direct || swapped)
}

# Apply the partner filter to one sample BND row. Returns the filtered
# `name_ST17_BND` string (sub-elements separated by '|' that don't
# partner-match the sample dropped). `score_ST17_BND` is passed through
# unchanged: AnnotSV's score join uses '|' at a different level than its
# name-join (one BED row's `name` field can itself contain '|' between
# gene-pair variants), so a 1:1 name↔score index alignment isn't safe.
# If the partner cannot be parsed from ALT, clear the name (conservative
# — a loose-end breakend can't be validated).
filter_bnd_st17_name <- function(sample_chrom, sample_pos, sample_alt,
                                  ref_names, tol = 10000) {
  cleaned <- strip_infotuple(ref_names)
  if (is.na(cleaned) || cleaned %in% c("", "NA", ".")) return("")

  partner <- parse_bnd_partner(sample_alt)
  if (is.na(partner$chrom)) return("")

  hits <- split_pipe_outside_parens(cleaned)

  # Per-hit format: chrA:posA-chrB:posB_(genes...)
  # Match the two coord pairs separated by '-'; anything after '_' is
  # gene-annotation suffix and ignored for partner validation.
  keep <- map_lgl(hits, function(hit) {
    m <- str_match(hit, "([^:|]+):([0-9]+)-([^:|]+):([0-9]+)")
    if (is.na(m[1, 2])) return(FALSE)
    bnd_pair_matches(
      sample_chrom, as.numeric(sample_pos), partner$chrom, partner$pos,
      m[1, 2], as.numeric(m[1, 3]),
      m[1, 4], as.numeric(m[1, 5]),
      tol = tol
    )
  })

  paste(hits[keep], collapse = "|")
}
```

```{r annotsv-user-cols-regex}
#  Derive the user-annotation column regex from AnnotSV header files 
# ANNOTSV_SETUPUSERANNO stages `<STn>_<basename>.header.tsv` files under
# annotsv_annotations/Annotations_Human/Users/<genome>/{FtIncludedInSV,
# SVincludedInFt,AnyOverlap}/. vembrane emits the corresponding INFO fields
# as `name_<STn>_<basename>` and `score_<STn>_<basename>` in the pipeline
# TSVs, so the "Custom Annot. Hits" tally in parse_annotsv() must only
# count columns backed by actual staged headers, not any incidental `_ST`
# prefix. `build_user_cols_regex()` reads those filenames at render time
# and builds the exact alternation regex; when the annotsv_annotations
# input isn't staged (e.g. dev-time render outside the pipeline), fall
# back to the structural `^(name|score)_ST\d+_` prefix pattern which still
# beats the pre-refactor `FtIncludedInSV|SVincludedInFt|AnyOverlap` regex.
build_user_cols_regex <- function() {
  users_root <- file.path("annotsv_annotations", "Annotations_Human", "Users")
  if (!dir.exists(users_root)) return("^(name|score)_ST\\d+_")
  hdr_files <- list.files(
    path       = users_root,
    pattern    = "\\.header\\.tsv$",
    recursive  = TRUE,
    full.names = FALSE
  )
  if (length(hdr_files) == 0) return("^(name|score)_ST\\d+_")
  basenames <- unique(sub("\\.header\\.tsv$", "", basename(hdr_files)))
  # Regex-escape literal chars (dot, paren, plus, etc.) so `.` in a
  # basename like `Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_AMP` matches a literal dot.
  escaped <- gsub("([][{}()*+?.\\\\^$|])", "\\\\\\1", basenames)
  sprintf("^(name|score)_(%s)$", paste(escaped, collapse = "|"))
}

user_cols_regex <- build_user_cols_regex()
```

```{r dt-readability, results='asis'}
# Cyborg theme renders the page in dark mode (black body, light grey text).
# DT tables inherit that styling and become unreadable (black on dark grey).
# Force the table cell area to white with dark text while keeping the
# surrounding chrome (filter / info / pagination / column-search) light so
# it stays readable against the dark page background.
cat('
<style>
  /*  Layout: width is handled per-DT-chunk via `#| column: screen-inset`
     (Quarto chunk option). This widens those specific chunks beyond the
     centered article body without overriding Bootstrap container widths
     elsewhere (which is fragile). Inside each chunk, force the DT widget
     and the table itself to fill 100% of the screen-inset region.  */
  .column-screen-inset .dataTables_wrapper,
  .column-screen-inset .datatables,
  .column-screen-inset .html-widget,
  .column-screen-inset table.dataTable { width: 100% !important; }

  /*  Typography: smaller section headers  */
  h1, .h1 { font-size: 1.6rem !important; }
  h2, .h2 { font-size: 1.3rem !important; margin-top: 1.2rem; }
  h3, .h3 { font-size: 1.1rem !important; margin-top: 1.0rem; }
  h4, .h4 { font-size: 1.0rem !important; }

  /*  Typography: smaller text inside DT tables  */
  table.dataTable, table.dataTable thead th, table.dataTable tbody td,
  .dataTables_wrapper, .dataTables_filter, .dataTables_length,
  .dataTables_info, .dataTables_paginate, .dt-buttons .dt-button {
    font-size: 0.80rem !important;
  }
  table.dataTable thead th, table.dataTable tbody td { padding: 4px 6px !important; }

  /*  Cell wrapping: allow long gene lists / coordinate strings to wrap
     instead of bulldozing horizontal layout. max-width caps cell width
     while word-break lets multi-element values break at any character.  */
  table.dataTable tbody td {
    white-space: normal !important;
    word-break: break-word !important;
    overflow-wrap: anywhere !important;
    max-width: 320px;
    vertical-align: top !important;
  }
  table.dataTable thead th {
    white-space: normal !important;
    vertical-align: bottom !important;
  }

  /*  Column grid lines: a 1 px right border on every td/th keeps headers
     visually aligned over their column values when the table wraps long
     strings into multi-line cells. Last column drops the right border so
     the table edge stays clean. Header row gets a heavier bottom border
     so the head/body boundary remains clear under the cyborg dark theme.  */
  table.dataTable td, table.dataTable th {
    border-right: 1px solid #ced4da !important;
  }
  table.dataTable td:last-child, table.dataTable th:last-child {
    border-right: none !important;
  }
  table.dataTable thead th {
    border-bottom: 2px solid #495057 !important;
  }

  /*  Theme: cell backgrounds (light) on the dark cyborg body  */
  table.dataTable { background-color: #ffffff !important; color: #212529 !important; }
  table.dataTable thead th,
  table.dataTable thead td { background-color: #e9ecef !important; color: #212529 !important;
                             border-bottom: 2px solid #adb5bd !important; }
  table.dataTable tbody tr td { background-color: #ffffff !important; color: #212529 !important; }
  table.dataTable tbody tr.odd td,
  table.dataTable.stripe tbody tr.odd > td,
  table.dataTable.display tbody tr.odd > td { background-color: #f1f3f5 !important; }
  table.dataTable tbody tr:hover td { background-color: #dee2e6 !important; }
  /* Per-column search row inside thead */
  table.dataTable thead input,
  table.dataTable thead select { background-color: #ffffff !important; color: #212529 !important;
                                 border: 1px solid #ced4da !important; }

  /* Wrapper chrome — keep light text against the dark page */
  .dataTables_wrapper { color: #f8f9fa !important; padding: 4px 0; }
  .dataTables_filter label,
  .dataTables_length label,
  .dataTables_info { color: #f8f9fa !important; }
  .dataTables_filter input,
  .dataTables_length select { background-color: #ffffff !important; color: #212529 !important;
                              border: 1px solid #ced4da !important; }
  .dataTables_paginate .paginate_button { color: #f8f9fa !important; }
  .dataTables_paginate .paginate_button.current,
  .dataTables_paginate .paginate_button:hover { background: #495057 !important;
                                                color: #ffffff !important; border-color: #6c757d !important; }
  /* CSV / Excel export buttons */
  .dt-buttons .dt-button { background-color: #495057 !important; color: #ffffff !important;
                          border: 1px solid #6c757d !important; }
</style>
')
```

```{r parse-annotsv}
annotsv_tsvs <- list.files(pattern = "\\.merged\\.annotated.*\\.tsv$",
                           full.names = TRUE)
# Exclude pass1/pass2 TSVs (also match the .tsv$ pattern but belong to
# the vembrane-table chunk below).
annotsv_tsvs <- setdiff(annotsv_tsvs,
                        list.files(pattern = "\\.filtered\\.pass[12]\\.tsv$",
                                   full.names = TRUE))

parse_annotsv <- function(tsv_path) {
  df   <- read_tsv(tsv_path, col_types = cols(.default = "c"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  full <- filter(df, Annotation_mode == "full")
  sample_id <- sub("\\.merged\\..+$", "", basename(tsv_path))
  acmg <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(full$ACMG_class))
  # `user_cols_regex` is built from the staged AnnotSV Users/ header files
  # (see annotsv-user-cols-regex chunk) so only actual user-annotation
  # columns count toward `Custom Annot. Hits`.
  user_cols <- grep(user_cols_regex, colnames(full), value = TRUE)
  custom_hits <- if (length(user_cols) > 0) {
    rowSums(!is.na(full[user_cols]) & full[user_cols] != "", na.rm = TRUE) > 0
  } else {
    rep(FALSE, nrow(full))
  }
  tibble(
    `Sample ID`             = sample_id,
    `Total SVs`             = nrow(full),
    `ACMG >= VUS (>=3)`     = sum(acmg >= 3, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Likely Pathogenic (4)` = sum(acmg == 4, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Pathogenic (5)`        = sum(acmg == 5, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Custom Annot. Hits`    = sum(custom_hits)
  )
}

stats_df <- map_dfr(annotsv_tsvs, parse_annotsv)
```

```{r merge-metadata}
# Join key is `id` (the pipeline meta.id, e.g. "colo829"), not `sample_id`
# (which is a friendly label like "sample_1" in the metadata CSV). `Sample ID`
# in stats_df is derived from the AnnotSV TSV filename and therefore matches
# `id` exactly. Strip leading/trailing whitespace from metadata column names —
# the test fixture has " mutations" (with a leading space) due to a CSV
# whitespace artifact.
metadata_file <- params$meta_data
if (!is.null(metadata_file) && nzchar(metadata_file) && file.exists(metadata_file)) {
  metadata <- read_csv(metadata_file, col_types = cols(.default = "c"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
  colnames(metadata) <- str_trim(colnames(metadata))
  stats_df <- left_join(stats_df, metadata, by = c("Sample ID" = "id"))
} else {
  metadata <- NULL
}

# Helper: attach sample_metadata rows to a variant table (SV / CNA / SNV) by
# joining on the pipeline id (`SAMPLE` in the variant df, `id` in the
# metadata CSV). Called twice per variant table:
#   * `cols = NULL` — full metadata merge, used before `write_tsv` so the
#     cohort TSVs carry every metadata column.
#   * `cols = "sample_id"` — DT-only merge to add the friendly sample_id
#     label without cluttering the interactive table with all cohort fields.
# Returns df unchanged when no metadata is available so downstream code is
# always safe to call.
merge_sample_metadata <- function(df, meta = metadata, sample_col = "SAMPLE",
                                   cols = NULL) {
  if (is.null(meta) || nrow(meta) == 0 || !sample_col %in% names(df)) return(df)
  m <- if (is.null(cols)) meta
       else dplyr::select(meta, id, dplyr::any_of(cols))
  m <- m |> dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  df |> dplyr::left_join(m, by = setNames("id", sample_col))
}
```

```{r link-columns}
knot_files <- list.files("knot", pattern = "\\.html$", full.names = FALSE)
xl_files   <- list.files("knot", pattern = "\\.xlsm$", full.names = FALSE)
vep_files  <- list.files("vep",  pattern = "\\.html$", full.names = FALSE)
igv_files  <- list.files("igv",  pattern = "\\.html$", full.names = FALSE)

# Bucketed IGV reports: IGV_REPORTS_SV emits one HTML per (sample × bucket)
# where bucket is {small, medium, large} is encoded in the filename.
# full `<sample>.pass2.igv.<bucket>` prefix so each bucket gets its own link.
make_link <- function(sample_id, files, subdir, label = "open &#x2197;",
                       suffix = NULL) {
  pat <- if (is.null(suffix)) {
    paste0("^", sample_id, "\\.")
  } else {
    paste0("^", sample_id, "\\.", suffix)
  }
  fname <- grep(pat, files, value = TRUE)
  if (length(fname) >= 1)
    sprintf('<a href="%s/%s" target="_blank">%s</a>', subdir, fname[1], label)
  else
    "-"
}

stats_df <- stats_df |>
  mutate(
    `KnotAnnotSV Report`   = map_chr(`Sample ID`, make_link, knot_files, "../annotations_sv/knotannotsv/html"),
    `KnotAnnotSV XLSM`     = if (length(xl_files) > 0)
                                map_chr(`Sample ID`, make_link, xl_files,
                                        "../annotations_sv/knotannotsv/xl",
                                        label = "download &#x2B07;")
                              else
                                "-",
    `VEP (breakpoint)`     = if (length(vep_files) > 0)
                                map_chr(`Sample ID`, make_link, vep_files, "../annotations_sv/ensemblvep/vep")
                              else
                                "-",
    `IGV small (<1 kb)`    = if (length(igv_files) > 0)
                                map_chr(`Sample ID`, make_link, igv_files, "../igv_reports",
                                        suffix = "pass2\\.igv\\.small")
                              else
                                "-",
    `IGV medium (1-10 kb)` = if (length(igv_files) > 0)
                                map_chr(`Sample ID`, make_link, igv_files, "../igv_reports",
                                        suffix = "pass2\\.igv\\.medium")
                              else
                                "-",
    `IGV large (>=10 kb)`  = if (length(igv_files) > 0)
                                map_chr(`Sample ID`, make_link, igv_files, "../igv_reports",
                                        suffix = "pass2\\.igv\\.large")
                              else
                                "-"
  )
```

```{r data-dict-loader, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Load per-variant-type VCF header dictionaries emitted by CREATE_DATA_DICT
# (one TSV per sample per variant type, from FILTER_{SV,CNA,SNV}). Union
# across samples and dedup by (field_type, field_name) — descriptions are
# stable across samples because they come from the same VCF-header block
# for a given caller + AnnotSV run.
load_data_dict <- function(subdir) {
  if (!dir.exists(subdir)) return(tibble::tibble())
  files <- Sys.glob(file.path(subdir, "*.data_dict.tsv"))
  if (length(files) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(files, readr::read_tsv,
                          show_col_types = FALSE,
                          col_types = "cccccc")) |>
    dplyr::distinct(field_type, field_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

dict_sv  <- load_data_dict("data_dict_sv")
dict_cna <- load_data_dict("data_dict_cna")
dict_snv <- load_data_dict("data_dict_snv")

# Hand-curated overlay for columns computed inside this qmd (not present
# in the VCF header). Overlay takes precedence over any VCF-header
# definition of the same name — the qmd-side meaning is the authoritative
# one for reviewers reading the DT tables. Do NOT paraphrase VCF-header
# entries here; if the truthful description lives in the header, let the
# dict TSV supply it.
qmd_computed_defs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~field_name,        ~description,
  "SAMPLE",           "VCF sample-column value (from the source caller output; may differ from cohort sample_id if the caller renamed the sample)",
  "sample_id",        "Cohort-facing sample identifier joined in from the params.sample_metadata CSV; NA when no metadata table was supplied",
  "driver_tier",      "Prioritization tier: T1 = empirical T-ALL recurrence (ST17/ST19) OR oncogenic in the candidate panel; T2 = candidate-gene hit; T3 = other pass2 evidence",
  "tier_score",       "Within-tier tie-breaker (recurrence count, candidate-gene count, or AnnotSV_ranking_score depending on tier)",
  "breakpoint",       "Compact chr:pos display of the record's primary breakpoint (SV/BND) or interval start (CNA)",
  "CytoBand_display", "chr<CHROM> prefix prepended to the AnnotSV CytoBand cell for a full-locus label",
  "Gene_name_display","Semicolon-joined unique SYMBOL list, dedup'd from AnnotSV's full-mode + per-split-mode Gene_name concatenation",
  "Candidate_genes",  "Intersection of Gene_name with the user candidate-gene panel (params.candidate_genes)",
  "has_mate",         "Whether both ends of a BND event survived the filter (TRUE = mate pair present, FALSE = orphaned BND)",
  "ST17_hit",         "One-line summary of the highest-scored SVTYPE-matched ST17 T-ALL recurrence BED hit(s)",
  "ST17_name",        "Top-3 ST17 hit names (by score), pipe-outside-parens joined",
  "ST17_score",       "Top-3 ST17 hit scores, paired positionally with ST17_name",
  "ST19_hit",         "One-line summary of the top 3 SVTYPE-matched ST19 T-ALL recurrent-CNV BED hits (AMP / DEL / GAIN / LOSS union, ordered by score desc; format: \"hit1 [s1]; hit2 [s2]; hit3 [s3]\")",
  "ST19_name",        "Top-3 ST19 hit names (score-ordered), pipe-joined; consolidated from name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_{AMP,DEL,GAIN,LOSS}",
  "ST19_score",       "Top-3 ST19 hit scores, paired positionally with ST19_name; consolidated from score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_{AMP,DEL,GAIN,LOSS}",
  "CNA_TYPE",         "Wakhan copy-number call type derived from CN1/CN2 (GAIN, LOSS, CNLOH); drives tier assignment and colour palette",
  "WAKHAN_TYPE",      "Raw Wakhan classification (integer/integer/cnloh/…), preserved from the caller",
  "CIViC_Consequence","VEP Consequence value from the CIViC INFO tag — compare to the top-level Consequence",
  "CIViC_SYMBOL",     "Gene symbol from the CIViC INFO tag — compare to the top-level SYMBOL",
  "CIViC_Variant_ID", "CIViC internal variant identifier",
  "CIViC_Variant_URL","Deep link to the variant page on civicdb.org",
  "CIViC_Entity_Variant_Origin", "CIViC assertion of variant origin (somatic / germline / unknown)",
  "CIViC_Entity_Therapies",      "Therapies linked to the variant per CIViC evidence entries",
  "CIViC_Assertion_ACMG_Codes",  "ACMG/AMP variant-classification codes attached to the CIViC assertion"
)

# Emit a small download-button HTML linking to the full data-dictionary TSV
# for a given variant type. Relative path resolves against index.html once
# both files are published under results/sv_report/ by publishDir.
# Returns "" when no dict TSV is present so the caller can `cat()` it
# unconditionally without leaking placeholders into the report.
dict_download_button <- function(subdir, label) {
  if (!dir.exists(subdir)) return("")
  files <- Sys.glob(file.path(subdir, "*.data_dict.tsv"))
  if (length(files) == 0) return("")
  # Use the first (should be the only) file. Relative link so it works both
  # in the raw index.html and via any static-file server.
  rel <- files[1]
  sprintf('<p style="margin:8px 0 4px 0;">
  <a href="%s" download
     style="display:inline-block; padding:8px 14px;
            background:#0d6efd; color:#ffffff; text-decoration:none;
            border-radius:5px; font-size:0.9em; font-weight:500;">
    &#x2B07;&#xFE0F; Download full %s data dictionary (TSV)
  </a>
  <span style="font-size:0.82em; color:#666; margin-left:8px;">
    Every VCF INFO / FORMAT / FILTER declaration for this variant type.
    Join by field_name to the cohort_%s.tsv output for column definitions.
  </span>
</p>
', rel, label, tolower(label))
}

# Render a compact "column definition" table for a display data frame.
# Priority: qmd-computed overlay first; then VCF-header dict lookup;
# blank when neither has a description (surfaces the gap to reviewers
# so it can be filled in the overlay).
render_data_dict <- function(display_df, dict_tbl, caption = NULL) {
  cols <- names(display_df)
  desc <- vapply(cols, function(c) {
    hit_ov <- qmd_computed_defs$description[qmd_computed_defs$field_name == c]
    if (length(hit_ov) > 0 && nzchar(hit_ov[1])) return(hit_ov[1])
    if (nrow(dict_tbl) > 0) {
      hit <- dict_tbl$description[dict_tbl$field_name == c]
      if (length(hit) > 0 && nzchar(hit[1])) return(hit[1])
    }
    ""
  }, character(1))
  ftype <- vapply(cols, function(c) {
    if (nrow(dict_tbl) > 0) {
      hit <- dict_tbl$field_type[dict_tbl$field_name == c]
      if (length(hit) > 0) return(hit[1])
    }
    ""
  }, character(1))
  ftype[!nzchar(ftype) & nzchar(desc)] <- "computed"
  ftype[!nzchar(ftype)]                <- "unknown"

  DT::datatable(
    tibble::tibble(Column = cols, Kind = ftype, Definition = desc),
    caption   = caption,
    filter    = "none", rownames = FALSE, width = "100%",
    options   = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 100, ordering = FALSE,
                     autoWidth = TRUE,
                     columnDefs = list(list(width = "18%", targets = 0),
                                       list(width = "10%", targets = 1)))
  )
}
```

```{r valuebox-helpers, include = FALSE}
# Value-box helper. Every KPI card uses vb_count(df_name, cond_fn) which
# guards against the referenced data frame being missing (branch turned off
# in the pipeline) or empty — yields 0 instead of throwing. cond_fn is a
# function of the data frame returning a logical vector; sum() collapses.
vb_count <- function(df_name, cond_fn) {
  if (!exists(df_name)) return(0L)
  df <- get(df_name)
  if (!is.data.frame(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(0L)
  tryCatch(as.integer(sum(cond_fn(df), na.rm = TRUE)),
           error = function(e) 0L)
}

# Defaults so the pure-markdown DISCO block on the Overview page can resolve
# its inline `r ...` references even when disco-plot-prep / disco-plot-data
# didn't fire (small cohorts with 0 Tier-1 records, or `disco_enable = FALSE`).
# These are OVERRIDDEN by the DISCO data chunks below when they do run —
# `<-` in a later chunk simply rebinds the name in the shared session.
pp_host           <- if (!is.null(params$proteinpaint_host)   && nzchar(params$proteinpaint_host))   params$proteinpaint_host   else "http://localhost:3456"
pp_genome         <- if (!is.null(params$proteinpaint_genome) && nzchar(params$proteinpaint_genome)) params$proteinpaint_genome else "hg38"
disco_mlst_json   <- "[]"
safe_cohort_label <- "Cohort"
n_cohort_snv      <- 0L
n_cohort_cna      <- 0L
n_cohort_bnd      <- 0L
n_cohort_samples  <- 0L
sample_ids        <- character(0)
lollipop_link_display <- tibble::tibble()
```
