```{r load-pass2}
# Load candidate-gene set unconditionally so downstream CNA / SNV chunks
# always see `candidate_set` — even when the SV pass2-clean chunk (which
# also assigns it) is skipped because pass2_long is empty.
candidate_set <- load_candidate_gene_set()

# SVTYPE / CNA_TYPE color palette (colorblind-safe Dark2 hues). Defined
# here unconditionally so the CNA pass2 DT chunk can reuse it even when
# the SV pass2-table chunk is skipped due to zero SV records.
svtype_colors <- c(
  BND = "#7570B3",  # purple
  DEL = "#D95F02",  # orange
  DUP = "#1B9E77",  # teal
  INS = "#E7298A",  # magenta
  INV = "#66A61E"   # green
)

pass2_files <- list.files(pattern = "\\.filtered\\.pass2\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)

# Also accept the synthetic test fixture
pass2_files <- c(pass2_files,
                 list.files(pattern = "vembrane_pass2_syndata\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE))

pass2_long <- if (length(pass2_files) > 0) {
  map_dfr(pass2_files, ~ read_tsv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = "c"),
                                  show_col_types = FALSE))
} else {
  tibble()
}

# vembrane's long-format prepends a SAMPLE column with the sample name from VCF
# FORMAT. Fall back to a filename-derived id if SAMPLE is absent (older outputs).
if (nrow(pass2_long) > 0 && !"SAMPLE" %in% names(pass2_long)) {
  pass2_long <- pass2_long |> mutate(SAMPLE = "unknown")
}

# Coerce numerics needed by plots
if (nrow(pass2_long) > 0) {
  pass2_long <- pass2_long |>
    mutate(
      ACMG_class_clean = acmg_factor(ACMG_class),
      ranking_score    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(scalar_first(AnnotSV_ranking_score)))
    )
}
```

```{r pass2-clean}
#| eval: !expr nrow(pass2_long) > 0

# Moved up from the DT chunk so plot-st17 counts and the sample-stats
# `Custom Annot. Hits` tally see the same partner-validated ST17 columns
# as the DT. The order matters:
#   1. Strip vembrane InfoTuple wrapping
#   2. Compute Candidate_genes from Gene_name 
#   3. Cast ACMG_class to integer 1-5
#   4. convert ST17 name/score cells whose SVTYPE suffix doesn't match the
#      record's SVTYPE 
#   5. BND partner-chromosome filter: keep ST17 BND name sub-elements
#      where both reference breakpoints match (within 10 kb).
pass2_long <- pass2_long |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), clean_tuple))

# Collapse AnnotSV's `full,split,split,...` padding on every character
# column (see clean_annot_padding docs). Runs after clean_tuple so any
# InfoTuple decoration is stripped first.
pass2_long <- pass2_long |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), \(v) vapply(v, clean_annot_padding, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)))

candidate_set <- load_candidate_gene_set()
# Union candidate-gene detection across Gene_name + Closest_left + Closest_right.
# The two Closest_* columns capture nearest-flanking genes when the SV falls
# in intergenic space — essential for BND breakpoints whose fusion partner
# is a driver gene that the SV interval itself doesn't overlap.
if (length(candidate_set) > 0 && "Gene_name" %in% names(pass2_long)) {
  closest_l <- if ("Closest_left"  %in% names(pass2_long)) pass2_long$Closest_left  else rep("", nrow(pass2_long))
  closest_r <- if ("Closest_right" %in% names(pass2_long)) pass2_long$Closest_right else rep("", nrow(pass2_long))
  pass2_long <- pass2_long |>
    mutate(Candidate_genes = pmap_chr(
      list(Gene_name, closest_l, closest_r),
      function(gn, cl, cr) compute_candidate_genes(gn, cl, cr, candidate_set)
    ))
} else {
  pass2_long$Candidate_genes <- ""
}

pass2_clean <- pass2_long |>
  mutate(ACMG_class = acmg_clean(ACMG_class)) |>
  select(-any_of("Annotation_mode"))

# Uniquify the ClinVar_SV_CLNSIG cell so a row overlapping 50 ClinVar records
# with the same "Pathogenic" label shows a single "Pathogenic" instead of a
# 50-element repeat wall.
if ("ClinVar_SV_CLNSIG" %in% names(pass2_clean)) {
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    mutate(ClinVar_SV_CLNSIG = vapply(ClinVar_SV_CLNSIG, clean_clinvar_clnsig,
                                     character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE))
}

# Round hVAF (HP1, HP2, unphased triple) to 2 decimal places so the DT reads
# "0.80,0.00,0.00" instead of "0.800000011920929,0.0,0.0".
if ("hVAF" %in% names(pass2_clean)) {
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    mutate(hVAF = vapply(hVAF, format_hvaf, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE))
}

# breakpoint column: "chr21:100000-110000" for intra-chromosomal, or
# "chr21:100000|chr5:300000" for interchromosomal BNDs.
if (all(c("CHROM", "POS", "ALT", "SVTYPE") %in% names(pass2_clean))) {
  end_col <- if ("END" %in% names(pass2_clean)) pass2_clean$END else pass2_clean$POS
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    mutate(breakpoint = compute_breakpoint(CHROM, POS, end_col, ALT, SVTYPE))
}

# Blank ST17 cells (name_ST17_* and score_ST17_*) whose suffix mismatches the record's SVTYPE. cur_column() extracts the suffix 
# convert the BND hits that intrachromosomal to be the intformation from the ST17 DEL, since ST17 BND is only interchromosomal translocations per authors definitions
pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
  mutate(intrachomosomal = purrr::map_lgl(.x = breakpoint, .f = ~chk_intra_bnd(.x))) |>
  mutate(name_ST17_BND = case_when(
    SVTYPE == "BND" & intrachomosomal == TRUE ~ name_ST17_DEL,
    TRUE ~ name_ST17_BND
  ), 
  score_ST17_BND = case_when(
    SVTYPE == "BND" & intrachomosomal == TRUE ~ score_ST17_DEL,
    TRUE ~ score_ST17_BND
  )) %>% 
  mutate(across(
    matches("^(name|score)_ST17_(BND|DEL|DUP|INS|INV)$"),
    ~ ifelse(SVTYPE == sub("^(name|score)_ST17_", "", cur_column()), as.character(.x), "")
  ))

# BND partner-chromosome filter (see helper docs in setup chunk).
if (all(c("name_ST17_BND", "CHROM", "POS", "ALT", "SVTYPE") %in% names(pass2_clean))) {
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    mutate(name_ST17_BND = pmap_chr(
      list(SVTYPE, CHROM, POS, ALT, name_ST17_BND),
      function(svt, chrom, pos, alt, nm) {
        if (svt != "BND") return(as.character(nm))
        filter_bnd_st17_name(chrom, pos, alt, nm)
      }
    ))
}

#  Driver-tier ranking + display-only columns 
# Compute one collapsed ST17 hit + score per row (SVTYPE-matched — the
# other 4 name_ST17_/score_ST17_ columns are already blanked by the earlier
# suffix-mismatch mutate). ST17_hit is empty when no ST17 evidence exists.
st17_name_col <- function(svt) {
  switch(svt,
         BND = "name_ST17_BND", DEL = "name_ST17_DEL",
         DUP = "name_ST17_DUP", INS = "name_ST17_INS",
         INV = "name_ST17_INV", NA_character_)
}
st17_score_col <- function(svt) sub("^name_", "score_", st17_name_col(svt))

pick_st17 <- function(df, picker) {
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) {
    col <- picker(df$SVTYPE[i])
    if (is.na(col) || !(col %in% names(df))) return("")
    val <- df[[col]][i]
    if (is.na(val)) "" else as.character(val)
  }, character(1))
}

pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
  mutate(
    ST17_name_raw  = pick_st17(pick(everything()), st17_name_col),
    ST17_score_raw = pick_st17(pick(everything()), st17_score_col)
  )

# Pair-split name + score together, dedup, order by score desc, truncate to
# top 3 hits. Both output columns keep the same ordering so the k-th name
# always pairs with the k-th score.
st17_pairs <- purrr::map2(pass2_clean$ST17_name_raw, pass2_clean$ST17_score_raw,
                          ~ parse_st17_pair(.x, .y, top_n = 3L))

pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
  mutate(
    ST17_name  = vapply(st17_pairs, `[[`, character(1), "names"),
    ST17_score = vapply(st17_pairs, `[[`, character(1), "scores"),
    # ST17_hit renders the top-3 pairs as "hit1 [s1]; hit2 [s2]; hit3 [s3]".
    # Blank when no ST17 evidence exists. When a score is missing (padded
    # NA slot from AnnotSV pipe-mismatch), the score bracket is omitted for
    # that entry.
    ST17_hit = vapply(seq_along(ST17_name), function(i) {
      nm <- ST17_name[i]; sc <- ST17_score[i]
      if (!nzchar(nm)) return("")
      nms <- split_pipe_outside_parens(nm)
      scs <- if (nzchar(sc)) str_split(sc, "\\|")[[1]] else rep("", length(nms))
      length(scs) <- length(nms)
      scs[is.na(scs)] <- ""
      pieces <- vapply(seq_along(nms), function(j) {
        if (nzchar(scs[j])) paste0(nms[j], " [", scs[j], "]") else nms[j]
      }, character(1))
      paste(pieces, collapse = "; ")
    }, character(1))
  ) |>
  select(-ST17_name_raw, -ST17_score_raw)

tier_tbl   <- assign_driver_tier(
  pass2_clean$ST17_name,
  pass2_clean$ST17_score,
  pass2_clean$Candidate_genes,
  pass2_clean$AnnotSV_ranking_score
)
pass2_clean <- bind_cols(pass2_clean, tier_tbl)

# Tier-3 MINDA-only filter. T3 records passed the pass2 gate on generic
# evidence (P_gain, RE_gene, ClinVar pathogenic, ACMG 3-5) but carry
# neither an ST17 T-ALL cohort hit (T1) nor a candidate-gene overlap (T2).
# For that tier, require consensus support: keep only records whose CALLER
# field indicates MINDA (Severus+SAVANA joint call), drop Severus-only
# T3 hits. T1/T2 are unaffected — biological drivers with clear evidence
# survive regardless of caller consensus, matching the pass2 filter's
# clause A rescue logic.
# CALLER field values seen in pipeline: "SEVERUS", "SAVANA", "MINDA".
# We match "MINDA" substring-inclusively (grepl) so future extensions like
# "MINDA;SEVERUS" or a comma-joined multi-call marker still pass.
#
# Defensive ST17 rescue: keep any record with a populated ST17_hit even
# if it lands in T3 under a future re-tiering (currently T3 excludes ST17
# hits by definition — they'd be T1 — but this guard makes the filter
# resilient to changes in assign_driver_tier() so a T-ALL recurrent hit
# is never silently dropped by the caller-consensus gate).
if ("CALLER" %in% names(pass2_clean)) {
  st17_present <- if ("ST17_hit" %in% names(pass2_clean)) nzchar(pass2_clean$ST17_hit)
                  else rep(FALSE, nrow(pass2_clean))
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    filter(!(driver_tier == 3L & !grepl("MINDA", CALLER, fixed = TRUE) & !st17_present))
}

# Dedup Gene_name so the cohort TSV holds "SYMBOL_A; SYMBOL_B" instead of
# AnnotSV's raw full-mode-`|`-joined + split-mode-`,`-repeated concatenation
# (e.g. "LOC1|LOC2|LOC3,LOC1,LOC2,LOC3"). Idempotent — already-clean strings
# round-trip. Keeps Gene_name usable as a stable output-CSV column while
# Gene_name_display remains the DT-friendly capped variant.
if ("Gene_name" %in% names(pass2_clean)) {
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    mutate(Gene_name = vapply(Gene_name, dedup_annot_multi,
                              character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE))
}

# Dedup CytoBand across full/split annotation modes. AnnotSV emits one
# cytoband per gene under split-mode, so multi-gene SVs produce runs like
# "q21.1-q21.3,q21.1,q21.1,q21.2,q21.2,q21.2,...". First dedup to the
# unique set; then collapse to a single "<min>-<max>" encompassing range
# via collapse_cytoband_range() so large SVs don't produce a 30+ band
# semicolon salad in the DT (matches the CNA-side treatment).
if ("CytoBand" %in% names(pass2_clean)) {
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    mutate(
      CytoBand = vapply(CytoBand, dedup_annot_multi,
                        character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
      CytoBand = vapply(CytoBand, collapse_cytoband_range,
                        character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
    )
}

# Cap the Gene_name display at 20 genes; append "(n=X genes)" annotation
# when capped so the reader knows the underlying multiplicity. Uses AnnotSV's
# Gene_count column as the authoritative gene tally.
pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
  mutate(Gene_name_display = pmap_chr(
    list(Gene_name, Gene_count),
    function(g, n) summarize_gene_list(g, n, cap = 20L)
  ))

# CytoBand display: prepend "chr<CHROM>" to the (already-deduped) band label
# so a clinician reads "chr9p21" instead of a bare "p21". Requires both CHROM
# and CytoBand present; leaves cells blank when either is missing.
if (all(c("CHROM", "CytoBand") %in% names(pass2_clean))) {
  pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
    mutate(CytoBand_display = ifelse(
      !is.na(CytoBand) & nzchar(CytoBand) & CytoBand != ".",
      paste0(ifelse(startsWith(as.character(CHROM), "chr"), as.character(CHROM),
                    paste0("chr", CHROM)),
             CytoBand),
      ""
    ))
}

# Optional EnsDb-based BND breakend gene annotation. Skips silently when
# params$ensembl_db is unset OR the file doesn't exist. Handles contigs
# that aren't in the EnsDb (chrUn_*, alt scaffolds, decoys) by filling
# `"unknown_contig:pos"` for the missing side instead of crashing the
# whole join. Vectorized over ALL breakpoints at once (no rowwise) so cost is
# O(N log M) not O(N * M): one `plyranges::join_overlap_inner` for breakpoints
# inside a gene, then one `GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest` for the remainder.
# Only trigger the (potentially slow) Bioc install when the EnsDb SQLite is
# actually staged — otherwise the annotation block would skip anyway.
if (!is.null(params$ensembl_db) && nzchar(params$ensembl_db) &&
    file.exists(params$ensembl_db)) {
  install_bioc_if_missing("ensembldb")
  install_bioc_if_missing("plyranges")
}

edb_annot_available <- !is.null(params$ensembl_db) &&
                        nzchar(params$ensembl_db) &&
                        file.exists(params$ensembl_db) &&
                        requireNamespace("ensembldb", quietly = TRUE) &&
                        requireNamespace("plyranges", quietly = TRUE)

if (edb_annot_available && nrow(pass2_clean) > 0 &&
    all(c("breakpoint", "SVTYPE", "ID") %in% names(pass2_clean))) {

  # Load EnsDb once. GENOME-wide EnsDb includes primary chromosomes 1-22/X/Y/MT.
  edb <- ensembldb::EnsDb(params$ensembl_db)
  # `canonical_transcript` and `gene_biotype` are needed beyond the gene label:
  # the ProteinPaint svfusion export needs an isoform accession per breakend, and
  # biotype is the tie-breaker below. ensembldb does not always surface every
  # underlying gene-table column, so degrade gracefully to gene_name only.
  ens_genes_gr <- tryCatch(
    ensembldb::genes(edb, columns = c("gene_id", "gene_name",
                                      "canonical_transcript", "gene_biotype")),
    error = function(e) {
      warning("EnsDb: canonical_transcript/gene_biotype unavailable (",
              conditionMessage(e), "); falling back to gene_name only.")
      ensembldb::genes(edb, columns = c("gene_id", "gene_name"))
    })
  for (cc in c("canonical_transcript", "gene_biotype")) {
    if (!cc %in% names(S4Vectors::mcols(ens_genes_gr)))
      S4Vectors::mcols(ens_genes_gr)[[cc]] <- NA_character_
  }
  # The overlap/nearest joins keep the QUERY strand ('*' from bp_in_gr), not the
  # subject's, so the gene's own strand must travel as a metadata column.
  ens_genes_gr$gene_strand <- as.character(BiocGenerics::strand(ens_genes_gr))
  # Some EnsDb rows have empty gene_name — fall back to gene_id so the
  # annotation always has a non-empty label.
  ens_genes_gr$gene_name <- ifelse(
    is.na(ens_genes_gr$gene_name) | !nzchar(ens_genes_gr$gene_name),
    ens_genes_gr$gene_id, ens_genes_gr$gene_name
  )
  ens_seqs <- as.character(GenomeInfoDb::seqlevels(ens_genes_gr))

  # Vectorized breakpoint parser — always emits TWO rows per record
  # (left + right anchor) regardless of SVTYPE. Downstream `pivot_wider`
  # produces `gene_name_left`, `distance_left`, `gene_name_right`,
  # `distance_right` columns for every record. Handles three breakpoint
  # shapes emitted by `compute_breakpoint()`:
  #   1. Interchromosomal BND        chrA:posA|chrB:posB
  #   2. Non-BND range (DEL/DUP/INV) chr:start-end
  #   3. Single-point (INS, or END==POS) chr:pos
  # In case (3) left == right (same position). Case (1) matches BND
  # SVTYPE; case (2) matches DEL/DUP/INV; case (3) matches INS or any
  # SVTYPE where END was missing / equal to POS.
  #
  # `distance` is 0 when the anchor is INSIDE the gene (gene_source == "overlap"),
  # positive if the anchor is outside (upstream of the left anchor =
  # negative offset from gene start / downstream of the right anchor =
  # positive offset from gene end). Kept as the raw absolute distance
  # in bp; the direction is implicit from which anchor (left / right).
  bp_split <- function(bp, sv, rid) {
    if (is.na(bp) || !nzchar(bp)) return(NULL)
    sides <- str_split(bp, "\\|")[[1]]

    # Case 1: interchromosomal BND (two |-separated chr:pos anchors)
    if (length(sides) == 2) {
      m1 <- str_match(sides[1], "^(chr[^:]+):([0-9]+)$")
      m2 <- str_match(sides[2], "^(chr[^:]+):([0-9]+)$")
      if (any(is.na(m1[1, ]) | is.na(m2[1, ]))) return(NULL)
      return(data.frame(
        ID       = c(rid, rid),
        side     = c("left", "right"),
        seqnames = c(sub("^chr", "", m1[1, 2]),
                     sub("^chr", "", m2[1, 2])),
        start    = as.integer(c(m1[1, 3], m2[1, 3])),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }

    # Case 2: non-BND range (DEL / DUP / INV) — one chr, two positions
    m <- str_match(sides[1], "^(chr[^:]+):([0-9]+)-([0-9]+)$")
    if (!is.na(m[1, 1])) {
      return(data.frame(
        ID       = c(rid, rid),
        side     = c("left", "right"),
        seqnames = sub("^chr", "", m[1, 2]),
        start    = as.integer(c(m[1, 3], m[1, 4])),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }

    # Case 3: single-point (INS with END==POS, or SVTYPE where END is
    # missing) — left == right. Distance columns will match on both sides.
    m <- str_match(sides[1], "^(chr[^:]+):([0-9]+)$")
    if (!is.na(m[1, 1])) {
      p <- as.integer(m[1, 3])
      return(data.frame(
        ID       = c(rid, rid),
        side     = c("left", "right"),
        seqnames = sub("^chr", "", m[1, 2]),
        start    = c(p, p),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }

    NULL
  }

  bp_df <- purrr::pmap(
    list(pass2_clean$breakpoint, pass2_clean$SVTYPE, pass2_clean$ID),
    bp_split
  ) |> purrr::compact() |> dplyr::bind_rows()

  if (nrow(bp_df) > 0) {
    bp_df$end <- bp_df$start + 1L
    # Split into in-EnsDb vs out-of-EnsDb before the join to avoid
    # 0-hit crashes for contigs like `chrUn_GL000219v1`.
    bp_in  <- bp_df |> dplyr::filter(seqnames %in% ens_seqs)
    bp_out <- bp_df |> dplyr::filter(!(seqnames %in% ens_seqs)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(gene_name = "unknown_contig", distance = NA_integer_)

    if (nrow(bp_in) > 0) {
      bp_in_gr <- plyranges::as_granges(bp_in)

      # TWO-STAGE ASSIGNMENT. `join_nearest` alone is NOT usable here: plyranges
      # documents it as returning an ARBITRARY nearest neighbour, and it offers no
      # multi-mapping option, so when a breakpoint sits inside several features it
      # discards the competitors BEFORE any tie-break can see them. The ordering
      # below was never wrong — it was being handed a one-row candidate set.
      #
      # Observed 2026-09-17, re-confirmed against EnsDb v110 on 2026-10-02:
      # chr9:131151786 lies inside BOTH NUP214 (ENSG00000126883, protein_coding,
      # chr9:131125573-131234663) and an unnamed lncRNA (ENSG00000236986,
      # chr9:131132852-131167505). join_nearest returned only the lncRNA, so
      # SET::NUP214 — the canonical T-ALL fusion from del(9)(q34.11q34.13) — was
      # emitted as SET::ENSG00000236986.
      #
      # Stage 1 uses join_overlap_inner (== find_overlaps), which emits one row per
      # (breakpoint, gene) pair, so every containing feature competes.
      # Stage 2 handles breakpoints in gene deserts, where there is nothing to
      # overlap, via distanceToNearest(select = "all") — the only API here that
      # returns ALL equidistant genes rather than one arbitrary pick.
      #
      # LRG_gene features are dropped at source. EnsDb carries LRG duplicates of
      # real genes (NUP214 is both ENSG00000126883 and LRG_1383 at near-identical
      # coordinates) whose canonical_transcript is an LRG accession such as
      # `LRG_482t1`. Those are neither RefSeq nor Ensembl, so they are rejected by
      # the ProteinPaint svfusion spec and degrade to a featureless box.
      ens_sel <- ens_genes_gr[
        is.na(ens_genes_gr$gene_biotype) | ens_genes_gr$gene_biotype != "LRG_gene"]
      ens_sel$gene_width <- BiocGenerics::width(ens_sel)
      ens_sel <- ens_sel[, c("gene_name", "canonical_transcript",
                             "gene_biotype", "gene_strand", "gene_width")]

      # Keep one row per (ID, side): downstream pivot_wider must produce atomic
      # character columns, not list-columns (which break coalesce in mlst_bnd).
      # Order: nearest, then protein_coding ahead of other biotypes, then an
      # official symbol ahead of a bare ENSG id (line ~1523 has already coalesced
      # an empty gene_name to gene_id, so the ENSG test does fire), then the
      # tightest gene interval LAST. Width must rank last and not earlier: the
      # lncRNA above is 34,653 bp against NUP214's 109,090 bp, so a width-first
      # rule actively prefers the wrong gene.
      .pick_one <- function(df) {
        df |>
          dplyr::arrange(ID, side, distance,
                         dplyr::coalesce(gene_biotype, "zzz") != "protein_coding",
                         startsWith(gene_name, "ENSG"),
                         gene_width) |>
          dplyr::distinct(ID, side, .keep_all = TRUE)
      }

      # ── Stage 1: every gene CONTAINING the breakpoint ──────────────────────
      ov <- plyranges::join_overlap_inner(bp_in_gr, ens_sel) |>
        tibble::as_tibble() |>
        dplyr::mutate(distance = 0L, gene_source = "overlap",
                      nearest_genes = NA_character_) |>
        dplyr::select(ID, side, gene_name, canonical_transcript, gene_biotype,
                      gene_strand, distance, gene_width, gene_source,
                      nearest_genes)

      # ── Stage 2: breakpoints with no containing gene -> ALL nearest ────────
      .done <- paste(ov$ID, ov$side)
      rest  <- bp_in_gr[!paste(bp_in_gr$ID, bp_in_gr$side) %in% .done]

      near <- ov[0, ]
      if (length(rest) > 0) {
        h <- GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest(rest, ens_sel, select = "all",
                                              ignore.strand = TRUE)
        if (length(h) > 0) {
          qi <- S4Vectors::queryHits(h); si <- S4Vectors::subjectHits(h)
          near <- tibble::tibble(
            ID                   = rest$ID[qi],
            side                 = rest$side[qi],
            gene_name            = ens_sel$gene_name[si],
            canonical_transcript = ens_sel$canonical_transcript[si],
            gene_biotype         = ens_sel$gene_biotype[si],
            gene_strand          = ens_sel$gene_strand[si],
            distance             = S4Vectors::mcols(h)$distance,
            gene_width           = ens_sel$gene_width[si],
            gene_source          = "nearest") |>
            # Report EVERY nearest gene, not just the one that wins the
            # tie-break: an intergenic breakpoint is only interpretable with its
            # flanking context. The primary columns stay atomic for pivot_wider;
            # this collapsed string is the full picture for the report.
            dplyr::group_by(ID, side) |>
            dplyr::mutate(nearest_genes = paste0(
              paste(sort(unique(gene_name)), collapse = ", "),
              " (", dplyr::first(distance), " bp)")) |>
            dplyr::ungroup()
        }
      }

      hits <- .pick_one(dplyr::bind_rows(ov, near)) |>
        dplyr::select(-gene_width)
    } else hits <- tibble::tibble(ID = character(), side = character(),
                                    gene_name = character(),
                                    canonical_transcript = character(),
                                    gene_biotype = character(),
                                    gene_strand = character(),
                                    gene_source = character(),
                                    nearest_genes = character(),
                                    distance = integer())

    bp_out_hits <- bp_out |>
      dplyr::mutate(canonical_transcript = NA_character_,
                    gene_biotype         = NA_character_,
                    gene_strand          = NA_character_,
                    gene_source          = "unknown_contig",
                    nearest_genes        = NA_character_) |>
      dplyr::select(ID, side, gene_name, canonical_transcript,
                    gene_biotype, gene_strand, distance, gene_source,
                    nearest_genes)
    all_hits <- dplyr::bind_rows(hits, bp_out_hits)

    # Every record now has a `left` and a `right` row (see bp_split
    # docs). Pivot to per-side gene / distance columns so every record
    # ends up with 4 new columns: gene_name_left, distance_left,
    # gene_name_right, distance_right.
    lr <- all_hits |>
      dplyr::filter(side %in% c("left", "right")) |>
      tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols     = ID,
                         names_from  = side,
                         values_from = c(gene_name, canonical_transcript,
                                         gene_strand, distance, gene_source,
                                         nearest_genes),
                         names_glue  = "{.value}_{side}")

    pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
      dplyr::left_join(lr, by = "ID") |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        # For BNDs the pair reads as a fusion (matches ST17_hit shape:
        # `GENE_A::GENE_B`). For non-BND records the two anchors are on
        # the same chromosome so use an ASCII arrow to show the local range.
        # ENSG identifiers are preserved when EnsDb had no HGNC symbol —
        # they carry biological meaning (pseudogene, lincRNA, novel locus)
        # and should not be silently masked. `unknown_contig` from the
        # bp_out fallback is passed through unchanged.

        edb_gene_pair = dplyr::case_when(
          SVTYPE == "BND" & !is.na(gene_name_left) & !is.na(gene_name_right) ~
            paste0(gene_name_left, "::", gene_name_right),
          !is.na(gene_name_left) & !is.na(gene_name_right) ~
            paste0(gene_name_left, " <-> ", gene_name_right),
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        # Compact distance summary — "L: 0 bp; R: 12503 bp" reads at a
        # glance; distance == 0 means the anchor lies inside the gene.
        edb_gene_distance = dplyr::case_when(
          !is.na(distance_left) & !is.na(distance_right) ~
            sprintf("L: %s bp; R: %s bp", distance_left, distance_right),
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        )
      )
  }
}

# has_mate — True when both _1 and _2 mates of a BND survive pass2.
# Simple: strip trailing `_1` / `_2` and count records per stripped ID.
# Non-BND records (no _1/_2 suffix) get has_mate = FALSE (mate concept
# doesn't apply). Useful for sort / filter in the DT: T1 BND records
# with has_mate=TRUE are the highest-confidence fusion calls.
pass2_clean <- pass2_clean |>
  group_by(ID_SHORT = str_remove(as.character(ID), "_[12]$")) |>
  mutate(has_mate = (SVTYPE == "BND" & dplyr::n() == 2L)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-ID_SHORT)

# Attach full sample_metadata (all cohort fields) so the cohort TSV carries
# clinical context — sex, age, EGIL, ETP, karyotype, driver fusions, ITD, etc.
# No-op when the metadata CSV wasn't supplied.
pass2_clean <- merge_sample_metadata(pass2_clean)

# Emit the cohort-level SV pass2 TSV (full schema, RE_gene retained,
# Closest_left/Closest_right + new driver_tier / tier_score / ST17_hit /
# Gene_name_display + CytoBand_display + has_mate columns included). The
# SV_REPORT_INDEX module declares `optional: true` on tsv_sv so the write
# being suppressed by the chunk-level guard is OK when pass2 is empty.
readr::write_tsv(pass2_clean, "cohort_sv_pass2.tsv", na = "NA")
```

```{r load-cna-pass2}
# CNA pass2 TSVs live under `cna_pass2/` to avoid colliding with the SV
# pass2 glob above — both file shapes end in `.filtered.pass2.tsv`.
# CN-specific columns: TCN/CN1/CN2/CNQ1/CNQ2/COV1/COV2 (vs. SV's VAF/hVAF/DR/DV)

cna_pass2_files <- list.files(
  path       = "cna_pass2",
  pattern    = "\\.filtered\\.pass2\\.tsv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

cna_pass2_long <- if (length(cna_pass2_files) > 0) {
  map_dfr(cna_pass2_files, ~ read_tsv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = "c"),
                                      show_col_types = FALSE))
} else {
  tibble()
}

if (nrow(cna_pass2_long) > 0 && !"SAMPLE" %in% names(cna_pass2_long)) {
  cna_pass2_long <- cna_pass2_long |> mutate(SAMPLE = "unknown")
}

# Derive a per-record CNA type from ALT (`<DUP>` -> "DUP") because SVTYPE in
# Wakhan VCFs is uniformly "CNV" and doesn't differentiate gain vs. loss.
if (nrow(cna_pass2_long) > 0) {
  cna_pass2_long <- cna_pass2_long |>
    mutate(
      CNA_TYPE         = str_remove_all(as.character(ALT), "[<>]"),
      ACMG_class_clean = acmg_factor(ACMG_class)
    )
}
```

```{r cna-pass2-clean}
#| eval: !expr nrow(cna_pass2_long) > 0


# write the cohort TSV 
cna_pass2_long <- cna_pass2_long |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), clean_tuple))

# Union candidate-gene detection across Gene_name + Closest_left + Closest_right
if (length(candidate_set) > 0 && "Gene_name" %in% names(cna_pass2_long)) {
  closest_l <- if ("Closest_left"  %in% names(cna_pass2_long)) cna_pass2_long$Closest_left  else rep("", nrow(cna_pass2_long))
  closest_r <- if ("Closest_right" %in% names(cna_pass2_long)) cna_pass2_long$Closest_right else rep("", nrow(cna_pass2_long))
  cna_pass2_long <- cna_pass2_long |>
    mutate(Candidate_genes = pmap_chr(
      list(Gene_name, closest_l, closest_r),
      function(gn, cl, cr) compute_candidate_genes(gn, cl, cr, candidate_set)
    ))
} else {
  cna_pass2_long$Candidate_genes <- ""
}

cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_long |>
  mutate(ACMG_class = acmg_clean(ACMG_class)) |>
  select(-any_of("Annotation_mode")) |>
  mutate(Gene_name_display = pmap_chr(
    list(Gene_name, Gene_count),
    function(g, n) summarize_gene_list(g, n, cap = 20L)
  ))

# breakpoint column: "chr21:13000002-31877979" for Wakhan CNA segments. Wakhan records are always intra-chromosomal
if (all(c("CHROM", "POS", "END", "ALT") %in% names(cna_pass2_clean))) {
  svtype_col <- if ("SVTYPE" %in% names(cna_pass2_clean)) cna_pass2_clean$SVTYPE else rep("CNV", nrow(cna_pass2_clean))
  cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
    mutate(breakpoint = compute_breakpoint(CHROM, POS, END, ALT, svtype_col))
}

# Parse WAKHAN_TYPE (GAIN / LOSS) from WAKHAN_ID's second colon-separated
# WAKHAN_ID format: "wakhan:GAIN:chr21:13000002-31877979".
# Falls back to the ALT-derived CNA_TYPE if WAKHAN_ID is missing 
if ("WAKHAN_ID" %in% names(cna_pass2_clean)) {
  cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
    mutate(WAKHAN_TYPE = case_when(
      !is.na(WAKHAN_ID) & nzchar(WAKHAN_ID) ~ str_split_fixed(WAKHAN_ID, ":", 3)[, 2],
      CNA_TYPE == "DUP" ~ "GAIN",
      CNA_TYPE == "DEL" ~ "LOSS",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ))
} else {
  cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
    mutate(WAKHAN_TYPE = case_when(
      CNA_TYPE == "DUP" ~ "GAIN",
      CNA_TYPE == "DEL" ~ "LOSS",
      TRUE ~ ""
    ))
}

# Summarize P_gain_source / P_loss_source / P_ins_source 
# DT shows the count and first-3 exemplars of each source
p_source_cols <- intersect(
  c("P_gain_source", "P_loss_source", "P_ins_source"),
  names(cna_pass2_clean)
)
if (length(p_source_cols) > 0) {
  cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
    mutate(across(all_of(p_source_cols),
                  ~ vapply(.x, summarize_p_source, character(1),
                           USE.NAMES = FALSE)))
}

#  ST19 name/score cells match the CNA type suffix (AMP/DEL/GAIN/LOSS) 
cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
  mutate(across(
    matches("^(name|score)_ST19_Alterations\\.CNV\\.Recurrent_(AMP|DEL|GAIN|LOSS)$"),
    function(col_vals) {
      suffix <- sub("^(name|score)_ST19_Alterations\\.CNV\\.Recurrent_", "",
                    cur_column())
      is_gain_like <- (WAKHAN_TYPE == "GAIN" | CNA_TYPE == "DUP")
      is_loss_like <- (WAKHAN_TYPE == "LOSS" | CNA_TYPE == "DEL")
      keep <- (is_gain_like & suffix %in% c("AMP", "GAIN")) |
              (is_loss_like & suffix %in% c("DEL", "LOSS"))
      ifelse(keep, as.character(col_vals), "")
    }
  ))

# CNA driver-priority tier 
cna_tier_tbl <- assign_driver_tier_cna(
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_AMP"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_DEL"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_GAIN"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_LOSS"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_AMP"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_DEL"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_GAIN"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_LOSS"]],
  cna_pass2_clean$Candidate_genes,
  cna_pass2_clean$AnnotSV_ranking_score
)
cna_pass2_clean <- bind_cols(cna_pass2_clean, cna_tier_tbl)

# Consolidate the 4 SVTYPE-matched ST19 name / score columns into a single
# top-3 hit summary — mirrors the ST17 pattern on the SV side (see the
# `pass2-clean` chunk). Rationale: the 8 raw ST19 columns are noisy (per-
# BED cells padded with `.,.,.` and misaligned between name and score
# order), which makes the DT hard to read. This block:
#   * Concatenates the 4 SVTYPE-matched `name_ST19_*` cells and the 4
#     `score_ST19_*` cells into pipe-joined raw strings (the earlier
#     SVTYPE-mismatch blanking has already left only the correct suffix
#     populated per record — GAIN+AMP for GAIN-like, DEL+LOSS for LOSS-like).
#   * Runs the same `parse_st17_pair()` helper (name-agnostic despite its
#     ST17 naming): splits by `|`, pairs by index, dedups by name,
#     orders by score desc, truncates to top-3.
#   * Emits three consolidated columns: `ST19_name`, `ST19_score`, and
#     `ST19_hit` (which renders "hit1 [s1]; hit2 [s2]; hit3 [s3]" for the DT).
# The raw 8 columns are retained in cna_pass2_clean for TSV export (they
# still land in cohort_cna_pass2.tsv) but dropped from the DT display below.
join_pipe_cells <- function(...) {
  parts <- as.character(c(...))
  parts <- parts[!is.na(parts) & nzchar(parts) & parts != "."]
  if (length(parts) == 0) return("")
  paste(parts, collapse = "|")
}

st19_name_raw <- mapply(
  join_pipe_cells,
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_AMP"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_DEL"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_GAIN"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["name_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_LOSS"]],
  USE.NAMES = FALSE
)
st19_score_raw <- mapply(
  join_pipe_cells,
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_AMP"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_DEL"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_GAIN"]],
  cna_pass2_clean[["score_ST19_Alterations.CNV.Recurrent_LOSS"]],
  USE.NAMES = FALSE
)

st19_pairs <- purrr::map2(st19_name_raw, st19_score_raw,
                          ~ parse_st17_pair(.x, .y, top_n = 3L))

cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
  mutate(
    ST19_name  = vapply(st19_pairs, `[[`, character(1), "names"),
    ST19_score = vapply(st19_pairs, `[[`, character(1), "scores"),
    ST19_hit   = vapply(seq_along(ST19_name), function(i) {
      nm <- ST19_name[i]; sc <- ST19_score[i]
      if (!nzchar(nm)) return("")
      nms <- split_pipe_outside_parens(nm)
      scs <- if (nzchar(sc)) str_split(sc, "\\|")[[1]] else rep("", length(nms))
      length(scs) <- length(nms)
      scs[is.na(scs)] <- ""
      pieces <- vapply(seq_along(nms), function(j) {
        if (nzchar(scs[j])) paste0(nms[j], " [", scs[j], "]") else nms[j]
      }, character(1))
      paste(pieces, collapse = "; ")
    }, character(1))
  )

# Same cleanup pass as SV: strip AnnotSV `full,split,split,...` padding
# from every character column, then dedup Gene_name / CytoBand across
# full/split modes, then compute CytoBand_display = "chr<CHROM><band>".
cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), \(v) vapply(v, clean_annot_padding, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)))

if ("Gene_name" %in% names(cna_pass2_clean)) {
  cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
    mutate(Gene_name = vapply(Gene_name, dedup_annot_multi,
                              character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE))
}

if ("CytoBand" %in% names(cna_pass2_clean)) {
  # Two-step cleanup: dedup_annot_multi() first turns the raw AnnotSV
  # full+split cell into a semicolon-joined unique-list; then
  # collapse_cytoband_range() folds that list to a single "<min>-<max>"
  # range so the DT shows "q23.31-q26.3" instead of 30+ semicolon-joined
  # sub-bands. Large-segment CNAs (very common on chr9p21, chr10q, etc.)
  # were the pain point that motivated this.
  cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
    mutate(
      CytoBand = vapply(CytoBand,       dedup_annot_multi,
                        character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE),
      CytoBand = vapply(CytoBand,       collapse_cytoband_range,
                        character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
    )
}

if (all(c("CHROM", "CytoBand") %in% names(cna_pass2_clean))) {
  cna_pass2_clean <- cna_pass2_clean |>
    mutate(CytoBand_display = ifelse(
      !is.na(CytoBand) & nzchar(CytoBand) & CytoBand != ".",
      paste0(ifelse(startsWith(as.character(CHROM), "chr"), as.character(CHROM),
                    paste0("chr", CHROM)),
             CytoBand),
      ""
    ))
}

cna_pass2_clean <- merge_sample_metadata(cna_pass2_clean)

readr::write_tsv(cna_pass2_clean, "cohort_cna_pass2.tsv", na = "NA")
```

```{r load-snv}

snv_files <- list.files(path = "snv", pattern = "\\.snv\\.filtered\\.tsv$",
                         full.names = TRUE)

snv_long <- if (length(snv_files) > 0) {
  map_dfr(snv_files, ~ read_tsv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = "c"),
                                show_col_types = FALSE))
} else {
  tibble()
}

if (nrow(snv_long) > 0 && !"SAMPLE" %in% names(snv_long)) {
  snv_long <- snv_long |> mutate(SAMPLE = "unknown")
}

# Coerce numerics needed by plots / filters
if (nrow(snv_long) > 0) {
  snv_long <- snv_long |>
    mutate(
      gnomADg_AF      = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gnomADg_AF)),
      CLAIRSTO_VAF    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(CLAIRSTO_VAF)),
      DEEPSOMATIC_VAF = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(DEEPSOMATIC_VAF))
    )
}
```

```{r snv-clean}
#| eval: !expr nrow(snv_long) > 0

# Candidate_genes: SYMBOL i∩ candidate gene panel
if (length(candidate_set) > 0 && "SYMBOL" %in% names(snv_long)) {
  snv_long <- snv_long |>
    mutate(Candidate_genes = ifelse(SYMBOL %in% candidate_set, SYMBOL, ""))
} else {
  snv_long$Candidate_genes <- ""
}

# Split the CIVIC INFO field into named columns for downstream review. Skips
# silently when the annotate_civic_snv step wasn't staged (no CIVIC column).
# The seven CIViC_* columns land immediately after the raw CIVIC column so
# reviewers can compare source and parsed values side-by-side.
if ("CIVIC" %in% names(snv_long)) {
  civic_parsed <- purrr::map(snv_long$CIVIC, parse_civic_field)
  civic_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
    CIViC_Consequence           = vapply(civic_parsed, `[[`, character(1), "CIViC_Consequence"),
    CIViC_SYMBOL                = vapply(civic_parsed, `[[`, character(1), "CIViC_SYMBOL"),
    CIViC_Variant_ID            = vapply(civic_parsed, `[[`, character(1), "CIViC_Variant_ID"),
    CIViC_Variant_URL           = vapply(civic_parsed, `[[`, character(1), "CIViC_Variant_URL"),
    CIViC_Entity_Variant_Origin = vapply(civic_parsed, `[[`, character(1), "CIViC_Entity_Variant_Origin"),
    CIViC_Entity_Therapies      = vapply(civic_parsed, `[[`, character(1), "CIViC_Entity_Therapies"),
    CIViC_Assertion_ACMG_Codes  = vapply(civic_parsed, `[[`, character(1), "CIViC_Assertion_ACMG_Codes")
  )
  snv_long <- dplyr::bind_cols(snv_long, civic_tbl)
}

# SNV driver-priority tier
snv_tier_tbl <- assign_driver_tier_snv(
  onc             = if ("ONC"             %in% names(snv_long)) snv_long$ONC             else rep(NA_character_, nrow(snv_long)),
  clnsig          = if ("CLNSIG"          %in% names(snv_long)) snv_long$CLNSIG          else rep(NA_character_, nrow(snv_long)),
  candidate_genes = snv_long$Candidate_genes,
  clairsto_vaf    = if ("CLAIRSTO_VAF"    %in% names(snv_long)) snv_long$CLAIRSTO_VAF    else rep(NA_character_, nrow(snv_long)),
  deepsomatic_vaf = if ("DEEPSOMATIC_VAF" %in% names(snv_long)) snv_long$DEEPSOMATIC_VAF else rep(NA_character_, nrow(snv_long))
)
snv_long <- bind_cols(snv_long, snv_tier_tbl)

snv_long <- merge_sample_metadata(snv_long)

# Emit cohort TSV (full schema, including columns not shown in DT). Optional
# output of the SV_REPORT_INDEX module.
readr::write_tsv(snv_long, "cohort_snv.tsv", na = "NA")
```

```{r disco-plot-prep}
#| eval: !expr isTRUE(params$disco_enable)

# ProteinPaint DISCO expects an `mlst` (mutation list) array with per-variant objects. Data-type (`dt`) codes: 1 = SNV point mutation, 2 = SV / fusion, 4 = CNV segment (log2 copy-number ratio as `value`).


#  SNV mlst 
disco_snv_class <- function(consequence) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(consequence) | !nzchar(consequence)                                             ~ "M",
    grepl("stop_gained|stop_lost|start_lost|nonsense", consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "N",
    grepl("frameshift",                                consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "F",
    grepl("splice",                                    consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "P",
    grepl("inframe_deletion",                          consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "D",
    grepl("inframe_insertion",                         consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "I",
    grepl("missense",                                  consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "M",
    grepl("synonymous",                                consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)   ~ "S",
    TRUE                                                                                  ~ "M"
  )
}

mlst_snv <- if (exists("snv_long") && nrow(snv_long) > 0 &&
                "driver_tier" %in% names(snv_long)) {
  snv_long |>
    dplyr::filter(driver_tier == 1L) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      dt       = 1L,
      chr      = if (all(startsWith(as.character(CHROM), "chr"))) as.character(CHROM)
                 else paste0("chr", CHROM),
      position = suppressWarnings(as.integer(POS)),
      ref      = REF,
      alt      = ALT,
      gene     = dplyr::coalesce(SYMBOL, "intergenic"),
      isoform  = dplyr::coalesce(Feature, "unknown"),
      mname    = dplyr::coalesce(HGVSp, HGVSc, ""),
      class    = disco_snv_class(Consequence),
      sample   = if ("sample_id" %in% names(snv_long))
                   dplyr::coalesce(sample_id, SAMPLE) else SAMPLE
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(position))
} else tibble::tibble()

#  CNA mlst 
mlst_cna <- if (exists("cna_pass2_clean") && nrow(cna_pass2_clean) > 0 &&
                "driver_tier" %in% names(cna_pass2_clean)) {
  cna_pass2_clean |>
    dplyr::filter(driver_tier == 1L) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      dt     = 4L,
      chr    = if (all(startsWith(as.character(CHROM), "chr"))) as.character(CHROM)
               else paste0("chr", CHROM),
      start  = suppressWarnings(as.integer(POS)),
      stop   = suppressWarnings(as.integer(END)),
      value  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(TCN)),
      # value = suppressWarnings(log2(pmax(as.numeric(TCN), 0.25) / 2))
      sample = if ("sample_id" %in% names(cna_pass2_clean))
                 dplyr::coalesce(sample_id, SAMPLE) else SAMPLE
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(start), !is.na(stop), !is.na(value))
} else tibble::tibble()

#  SV BND mlst
# Partner chr + pos parsed from ALT bracket notation via `parse_bnd_partner()`.
# `geneA` / `geneB` (record-side and partner-side gene) come from the bp_split
# EnsDb annotation earlier in the pipeline: `gene_name_left` is the anchor at
# CHROM:POS and `gene_name_right` is the partner anchor. Fall back to
# AnnotSV/VEP-derived `Gene_name` / `Closest_left` for `geneA` and "unknown"
# for `geneB` when the EnsDb block didn't run (e.g. rocker/verse image without
# ensembldb + plyranges).
mlst_bnd <- if (exists("pass2_clean") && nrow(pass2_clean) > 0 &&
                "driver_tier" %in% names(pass2_clean)) {
  bnd_t1 <- pass2_clean |>
    dplyr::filter(driver_tier == 1L, SVTYPE == "BND")
  if (nrow(bnd_t1) > 0) {
    partners  <- lapply(bnd_t1$ALT, parse_bnd_partner)
    prefix_chr <- function(c) ifelse(is.na(c) | !nzchar(c) | startsWith(c, "chr"),
                                     c, paste0("chr", c))
    gene_left  <- if ("gene_name_left"  %in% names(bnd_t1)) bnd_t1$gene_name_left
                  else rep(NA_character_, nrow(bnd_t1))
    gene_right <- if ("gene_name_right" %in% names(bnd_t1)) bnd_t1$gene_name_right
                  else rep(NA_character_, nrow(bnd_t1))
    sample_lbl <- if ("sample_id" %in% names(bnd_t1))
                    dplyr::coalesce(bnd_t1$sample_id, bnd_t1$SAMPLE)
                  else bnd_t1$SAMPLE
    dplyr::tibble(
      dt      = 2L,
      chrA    = prefix_chr(as.character(bnd_t1$CHROM)),
      posA    = suppressWarnings(as.integer(bnd_t1$POS)),
      geneA   = dplyr::coalesce(gene_left, bnd_t1$Gene_name,
                                bnd_t1$Closest_left, "intergenic"),
      # parse_bnd_partner strips the "chr" prefix via normalize_chrom() —
      # re-prepend it here since DISCO expects "chrN" format.
      chrB    = prefix_chr(vapply(partners, function(p) as.character(p$chrom),
                                  character(1))),
      posB    = vapply(partners, function(p) suppressWarnings(as.integer(p$pos)),
                       integer(1)),
      geneB   = dplyr::coalesce(gene_right, "unknown"),
      strandA = "+",
      strandB = "-",
      sample  = sample_lbl
    ) |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(posA), !is.na(chrB), !is.na(posB))
  } else tibble::tibble()
} else tibble::tibble()

# Combine as a single mlst list — but transpose EACH subset first so per-
# record named lists only carry that dt's own fields. bind_rows() would
# NA-pad missing columns (SNV records would get chrA/posA/geneA=NA, CNA
# records would get chr/position/gene=NA, etc.) and jsonlite serializes
# those as literal `null` which ProteinPaint DISCO rejects as malformed
# records. Per-subset transpose keeps each dt's payload minimal.
df_to_records <- function(df) {
  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(list())
  purrr::transpose(df)
}
mlst_all_list <- c(
  df_to_records(mlst_snv),
  df_to_records(mlst_cna),
  df_to_records(mlst_bnd)
)

# Keep `mlst_all` as a tibble for the status-count chunk below (`sum(dt==1)`
# etc.); the JSON step uses `mlst_all_list` for the record-level output.
mlst_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(mlst_snv, mlst_cna, mlst_bnd)
```

```{r disco-plot-data, include = FALSE}
#| eval: !expr isTRUE(params$disco_enable) && exists("mlst_all") && nrow(mlst_all) > 0

# DATA-ONLY chunk. This chunk produces no rendered output; it exposes a
# handful of variables (disco_mlst_json, safe_cohort_label, pp_host,
# pp_genome, n_cohort_snv/cna/bnd, n_cohort_samples) that the pure-markdown
# runproteinpaint block below then consumes via knitr inline `r ...`
# expressions. Separating data from presentation this way keeps the
# runproteinpaint template inspectable as real HTML/JS with syntax
# highlighting instead of a sprintf-embedded string blob.
#
# Layout produced by this chunk + the markdown below:
#   * ONE cohort DISCO plot rendered inline in the report body (single
#     `<div id="disco_pp_cohort">` mount + runproteinpaint call). Contains
#     the union of Tier-1 records across every sample.
#   * Per-sample DISCO HTMLs written to `protein_paint_out/` (still
#     managed by this chunk via build_disco_html + writeLines) for
#     sample-scoped inspection outside the main report.
# No top-level `disco_plot.html` file is written any more — the report
# itself IS the cohort plot.

pp_host   <- if (!is.null(params$proteinpaint_host)   && nzchar(params$proteinpaint_host))   params$proteinpaint_host   else "http://localhost:3456"
pp_genome <- if (!is.null(params$proteinpaint_genome) && nzchar(params$proteinpaint_genome)) params$proteinpaint_genome else "hg38"

# Sanitize label for safe use as a filename component: letters, digits,
# dot, underscore, hyphen — anything else becomes underscore.
disco_sample_slug <- function(s) {
  s <- as.character(s)
  s[is.na(s) | !nzchar(s)] <- "unknown"
  gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", s)
}

# Build the full standalone HTML document for a per-sample DISCO plot.
# Only used for the per-sample files under protein_paint_out/. The cohort
# plot is rendered inline in this document; nothing here is emitted for it.
build_disco_html <- function(mlst_records, ring_label) {
  mlst_records <- lapply(mlst_records, function(rec) rec[names(rec) != "sample"])
  mlst_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(mlst_records, auto_unbox = TRUE, na = "null")
  safe_label <- gsub('"', '\\"', gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", as.character(ring_label)), fixed = TRUE)
  sprintf('<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>DISCO plot — %s</title>
  <style>
    body { margin: 0; padding: 12px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; background: #ffffff; }
    #disco_pp_holder { min-height: 700px; width: 100%%; }
  </style>
  <script src="https://proteinpaint.stjude.org/bin/proteinpaint.js" charset="utf-8"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <div id="disco_pp_holder"></div>
  <script>
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
      if (typeof runproteinpaint !== "function") {
        document.getElementById("disco_pp_holder").innerHTML =
          "<em>ProteinPaint JS bundle failed to load. Verify network access to proteinpaint.stjude.org or host a local mirror.</em>";
        return;
      }
      runproteinpaint({
        host: "%s",
        holder: document.getElementById("disco_pp_holder"),
        noheader: true,
        nobox: true,
        genome: "%s",
        disco: {
          mlst: %s,
          settings: { Disco: { centerText: "%s" } }
        }
      });
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
', safe_label, pp_host, pp_genome, mlst_json, safe_label)
}

# Partition records by sample for per-sample HTMLs.
sample_of <- function(rec) {
  v <- rec[["sample"]]
  if (is.null(v) || is.na(v) || !nzchar(as.character(v))) "unknown" else as.character(v)
}
per_sample_labels  <- vapply(mlst_all_list, sample_of, character(1))
per_sample_split   <- split(mlst_all_list, per_sample_labels)
sample_ids         <- names(per_sample_split)
sample_slugs       <- disco_sample_slug(sample_ids)
n_cohort_samples   <- length(sample_ids)

# Braces required: R's parser closes the outer `if (…) expr` before it
# reaches the naked `else` on the next line, so the chained form must
# be `if {…} else if {…} else {…}` when broken across lines.
cohort_label <- if (n_cohort_samples > 1) {
  sprintf("Cohort (n = %d)", n_cohort_samples)
} else if (n_cohort_samples == 1) {
  sample_ids[1]
} else {
  "Cohort"
}

# Per-sample DISCO HTMLs → protein_paint_out/.
dir.create("protein_paint_out", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
sample_files <- file.path("protein_paint_out",
                          paste0("disco_plot_", sample_slugs, ".html"))
for (i in seq_along(sample_ids)) {
  writeLines(
    build_disco_html(per_sample_split[[i]], sample_ids[i]),
    sample_files[i]
  )
}

# ── Values consumed by the pure-markdown runproteinpaint block below via
# inline `r ...` expressions. Every hand-off is a single scalar / atomic
# string so knitr's inline substitution rules apply cleanly (multi-line
# HTML is emitted as pure markdown text, not through this data chunk).
n_cohort_snv <- sum(mlst_all$dt == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
n_cohort_cna <- sum(mlst_all$dt == 4, na.rm = TRUE)
n_cohort_bnd <- sum(mlst_all$dt == 2, na.rm = TRUE)

# Drop the per-record `sample` field before serializing — DISCO's adhoc
# launcher ignores unknown keys but stripping keeps the embedded JSON minimal.
disco_mlst_prep <- lapply(mlst_all_list, function(rec) rec[names(rec) != "sample"])
disco_mlst_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(disco_mlst_prep, auto_unbox = TRUE, na = "null")

# Escape backslash + double-quote so the label is safe inside a JS string literal.
safe_cohort_label <- gsub('"', '\\"',
                          gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", as.character(cohort_label)),
                          fixed = TRUE)
```

```{r lollipop-plot-data, include = FALSE}
#| eval: !expr isTRUE(params$disco_enable) && exists("snv_long") && nrow(snv_long) > 0 && "driver_tier" %in% names(snv_long)

# Filter to Tier-1 SNVs with a resolvable gene SYMBOL that can project onto
# a coding-region protein. See earlier lollipop-plot-embed comment for the
# rationale on is_protein_projectable (CSDE1 vs NRAS at chr1:114716126 case).
tier1_snv <- dplyr::filter(snv_long, driver_tier == 1L)
pp_host   <- if (!is.null(params$proteinpaint_host)   && nzchar(params$proteinpaint_host))   params$proteinpaint_host   else "http://localhost:3456"
pp_genome <- if (!is.null(params$proteinpaint_genome) && nzchar(params$proteinpaint_genome)) params$proteinpaint_genome else "hg38"

snv_class_from_consequence <- if (exists("disco_snv_class")) {
  disco_snv_class
} else {
  function(c) "M"
}

is_protein_projectable <- function(hgvsp, consequence) {
  hgvsp_ok <- !is.na(hgvsp) & nzchar(hgvsp)
  cons_ok  <- !is.na(consequence) & nzchar(consequence) &
              grepl(paste0("missense|stop_gained|stop_lost|start_lost|",
                           "frameshift|inframe_|splice_(acceptor|donor|region)|",
                           "protein_altering|synonymous|nonsense"),
                    consequence, ignore.case = TRUE)
  hgvsp_ok | cons_ok
}

lollipop_variants <- if (nrow(tier1_snv) == 0) tibble::tibble() else {
  n_r         <- nrow(tier1_snv)
  sample_col  <- if ("sample_id" %in% names(tier1_snv)) "sample_id" else "SAMPLE"
  sample_vals <- as.character(tier1_snv[[sample_col]])
  sample_vals <- ifelse(is.na(sample_vals) | !nzchar(sample_vals), "unknown", sample_vals)
  clnsig_vals <- if ("CLNSIG" %in% names(tier1_snv)) as.character(tier1_snv$CLNSIG) else rep(NA_character_, n_r)
  onc_vals    <- if ("ONC"    %in% names(tier1_snv)) as.character(tier1_snv$ONC)    else rep(NA_character_, n_r)
  clnsig_vals[!nzchar(clnsig_vals) | clnsig_vals == "."] <- NA_character_
  onc_vals   [!nzchar(onc_vals)    | onc_vals    == "."] <- NA_character_
  pathogenicity_vals <- dplyr::coalesce(clnsig_vals, onc_vals, "")
  c_vaf <- if ("CLAIRSTO_VAF"    %in% names(tier1_snv)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(tier1_snv$CLAIRSTO_VAF)) else rep(NA_real_, n_r)
  d_vaf <- if ("DEEPSOMATIC_VAF" %in% names(tier1_snv)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(tier1_snv$DEEPSOMATIC_VAF)) else rep(NA_real_, n_r)
  vaf_max <- pmax(c_vaf, d_vaf, na.rm = FALSE)
  vaf_max <- ifelse(is.na(vaf_max), dplyr::coalesce(c_vaf, d_vaf), vaf_max)
  vaf_vals <- ifelse(is.na(vaf_max), "", sprintf("%.3f", vaf_max))
  consequence_vals <- if ("Consequence" %in% names(tier1_snv)) as.character(tier1_snv$Consequence) else rep("", n_r)
  hgvsp_col <- if ("HGVSp" %in% names(tier1_snv)) as.character(tier1_snv$HGVSp) else rep(NA_character_, n_r)

  tier1_snv |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      gene_symbol = dplyr::coalesce(SYMBOL, NA_character_),
      chr    = if (all(startsWith(as.character(CHROM), "chr"))) as.character(CHROM)
               else paste0("chr", CHROM),
      pos    = suppressWarnings(as.integer(POS)),
      mname  = dplyr::coalesce(HGVSp, HGVSc, ""),
      class  = snv_class_from_consequence(Consequence),
      dt     = 1L,
      ref    = REF, alt = ALT, sample = sample_vals,
      Consequence   = consequence_vals,
      Pathogenicity = pathogenicity_vals,
      VAF           = vaf_vals,
      .hgvsp_raw    = hgvsp_col
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(pos), !is.na(gene_symbol), nzchar(gene_symbol),
                  is_protein_projectable(.hgvsp_raw, Consequence)) |>
    dplyr::select(-.hgvsp_raw)
}

build_lollipop_variants_json <- function(variants_df) {
  info_cols <- intersect(c("Consequence", "Pathogenicity", "VAF"), names(variants_df))
  top_cols  <- setdiff(names(variants_df), c("gene_symbol", info_cols))
  is_empty_scalar <- function(v) {
    if (is.null(v)) return(TRUE)
    if (length(v) != 1) return(FALSE)
    if (is.na(v)) return(TRUE)
    if (is.character(v) && !nzchar(v)) return(TRUE)
    FALSE
  }
  vars <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(variants_df)), function(i) {
    top_part  <- as.list(variants_df[i, top_cols,  drop = FALSE])
    info_part <- as.list(variants_df[i, info_cols, drop = FALSE])
    info_part <- info_part[!vapply(info_part, is_empty_scalar, logical(1))]
    if (length(info_part) > 0) top_part$info <- info_part
    top_part
  })
  jsonlite::toJSON(vars, auto_unbox = TRUE, na = "null")
}

build_lollipop_html <- function(gene, variants_df) {
  vars_json <- build_lollipop_variants_json(variants_df)
  safe_gene <- gsub('"', '\\"', gene, fixed = TRUE)
  sprintf('<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Lollipop &mdash; %s (Tier-1 SNVs)</title>
  <style>
    body { margin: 0; padding: 12px; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; background: #ffffff; }
    #lollipop_pp_holder { min-height: 500px; width: 100%%; }
  </style>
  <script src="https://proteinpaint.stjude.org/bin/proteinpaint.js" charset="utf-8"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <div id="lollipop_pp_holder"></div>
  <script>
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
      if (typeof runproteinpaint !== "function") {
        document.getElementById("lollipop_pp_holder").innerHTML =
          "<em>ProteinPaint JS bundle failed to load. Verify network access to proteinpaint.stjude.org or host a local mirror.</em>";
        return;
      }
      runproteinpaint({
        host: "%s",
        holder: document.getElementById("lollipop_pp_holder"),
        parseurl: true, noheader: true, nobox: true,
        genome: "%s",
        gene: "%s",
        tracks: [ { type: "mds3", name: "Tier-1 SNVs %s", custom_variants: %s } ]
      });
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
', safe_gene, pp_host, pp_genome, safe_gene, safe_gene, vars_json)
}

# Sanitize label for filename
if (!exists("disco_sample_slug")) {
  disco_sample_slug <- function(s) {
    s <- as.character(s)
    s[is.na(s) | !nzchar(s)] <- "unknown"
    gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", s)
  }
}

lollipop_link_display <- if (nrow(lollipop_variants) == 0) tibble::tibble() else {
  dir.create("protein_paint_out", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  gene_counts <- lollipop_variants |>
    dplyr::group_by(gene_symbol) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_snv       = dplyr::n(),
      top_variant = {
        vaf_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(VAF))
        mname[order(-vaf_num, na.last = TRUE)][1]
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(desc(n_snv), gene_symbol)

  lollipop_files <- character(nrow(gene_counts))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(gene_counts))) {
    g   <- gene_counts$gene_symbol[i]
    vg  <- dplyr::filter(lollipop_variants, gene_symbol == g)
    out <- file.path("protein_paint_out",
                     sprintf("lollipop_%s.html", disco_sample_slug(g)))
    writeLines(build_lollipop_html(g, vg), out)
    lollipop_files[i] <- out
  }
  tibble::tibble(
    Gene         = sprintf('<a href="%s" target="_blank" rel="noopener">%s</a>',
                           lollipop_files, gene_counts$gene_symbol),
    `# Tier-1`   = gene_counts$n_snv,
    `Top variant` = ifelse(is.na(gene_counts$top_variant) | !nzchar(gene_counts$top_variant),
                          "&mdash;", gene_counts$top_variant),
    Open         = sprintf('<a href="%s" target="_blank" rel="noopener">&#128279;</a>',
                          lollipop_files)
  )
}
```

## Row {.fill}

### SV Protein Paint {title="SV Protein Paint (gene fusion)"}

```{r sv-proteinpaint-build}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

# ── ProteinPaint svfusion export ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Renders Tier 1 + Tier 2 SVs as a two-breakpoint fusion table for the
# ProteinPaint gene-fusion app (https://proteinpaint.stjude.org/?appcard=genefusion,
# or the FusionEditor at /FusionEditor/). Format spec:
# https://docs.stjude.cloud/visualization-community/proteinpaint/sv-and-fusion-transcript
#
# THREE THINGS THE SPEC REQUIRES THAT THE PASS2 TABLE DOES NOT ALREADY SATISFY:
#   1. positions are 0-BASED   -> POS - 1 (VCF POS is 1-based)
#   2. chromosomes need "chr"  -> raw CHROM is bare ("21")
#   3. one row per EVENT       -> an interchromosomal BND is TWO VCF records
#                                 (both breakends); emitting both duplicates it
#
# 5'/3' ASSIGNMENT comes from the ALT bracket orientation, NOT from POS order.
# VCF 4.2 breakend forms:  t[p[ and t]p]  -> THIS record is 5'
#                          ]p]t and [p[t  -> the PARTNER is 5'
# i.e. an ALT beginning with the ref base means this side is 5'. Both mates of a
# pair independently agree on the assignment, so dedup may keep either one.
#
# INS is excluded: END == POS gives no second breakpoint, and ProteinPaint's
# model is two joined breakpoints. (The spec's "inserted segment" is a different
# concept — sequence between two breakpoints in an RNA-seq fusion.)
pp_sv_fusion      <- NULL
pp_sv_note        <- NULL
pp_sv_input_json  <- "null"   # JS-safe string of the whole svfusion file

.need <- c("SAMPLE", "CHROM", "POS", "END", "ALT", "SVTYPE", "driver_tier")
if (exists("pass2_clean") && is.data.frame(pass2_clean) &&
    nrow(pass2_clean) > 0 && all(.need %in% names(pass2_clean))) {

  .pfx <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(x) | startsWith(x, "chr"),
                             x, paste0("chr", x))
  # gene / isoform / strand per side come from the EnsDb join above. They are
  # absent when params$ensembl_db is unset — fall back to blanks, which the
  # spec permits (renders an intergenic box rather than a protein).
  .col <- function(nm) if (nm %in% names(pass2_clean)) as.character(pass2_clean[[nm]]) else NA_character_

  .d <- tibble::tibble(
    SAMPLE = as.character(pass2_clean$SAMPLE),
    CHROM  = as.character(pass2_clean$CHROM),
    POS    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(pass2_clean$POS)),
    END    = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(pass2_clean$END)),
    ALT    = as.character(pass2_clean$ALT),
    SVTYPE = as.character(pass2_clean$SVTYPE),
    tier   = suppressWarnings(as.integer(pass2_clean$driver_tier)),
    g_l    = .col("gene_name_left"),            g_r = .col("gene_name_right"),
    t_l    = .col("canonical_transcript_left"), t_r = .col("canonical_transcript_right"),
    s_l    = .col("gene_strand_left"),          s_r = .col("gene_strand_right"),
    DV     = .col("DV")
  ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(tier), tier %in% c(1L, 2L)) |>
    dplyr::filter(SVTYPE != "INS")

  if (nrow(.d) > 0) {
    .m     <- stringr::str_match(.d$ALT, "[\\[\\]]([^:\\[\\]]+):([0-9]+)[\\[\\]]")
    .isbnd <- .d$SVTYPE == "BND" | grepl("[\\[\\]]", .d$ALT)
    .ok    <- !is.na(.m[, 2])
    .five  <- grepl("^[ACGTNacgtn]", .d$ALT)      # this record is the 5' side

    .d <- .d |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        .bnd = .isbnd & .ok,
        chr_a = .pfx(ifelse(.bnd & !.five, .m[, 2], CHROM)),
        pos_a = ifelse(.bnd & !.five, suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.m[, 3])), POS),
        gen_a = ifelse(.bnd & !.five, g_r, g_l),
        iso_a = ifelse(.bnd & !.five, t_r, t_l),
        str_a = ifelse(.bnd & !.five, s_r, s_l),
        chr_b = .pfx(ifelse(.bnd, ifelse(.five, .m[, 2], CHROM), CHROM)),
        pos_b = ifelse(.bnd, ifelse(.five, suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.m[, 3])), POS), END),
        gen_b = ifelse(.bnd & !.five, g_l, g_r),
        iso_b = ifelse(.bnd & !.five, t_l, t_r),
        str_b = ifelse(.bnd & !.five, s_l, s_r)
      ) |>
      # drop non-BND records that have no usable second breakpoint
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(pos_a), !is.na(pos_b), pos_a != pos_b | .bnd) |>
      # one row per event: collapse the two breakends of a BND pair
      dplyr::mutate(.key = paste(SAMPLE,
                                 pmin(paste0(chr_a, ":", pos_a), paste0(chr_b, ":", pos_b)),
                                 pmax(paste0(chr_a, ":", pos_a), paste0(chr_b, ":", pos_b)))) |>
      dplyr::distinct(.key, .keep_all = TRUE)

    pp_sv_fusion <- .d |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        gene_a = dplyr::coalesce(gen_a, ""), isoform_a = dplyr::coalesce(iso_a, ""),
        chr_a, position_a = as.integer(pos_a - 1), strand_a = dplyr::coalesce(str_a, "+"),
        gene_b = dplyr::coalesce(gen_b, ""), isoform_b = dplyr::coalesce(iso_b, ""),
        chr_b, position_b = as.integer(pos_b - 1), strand_b = dplyr::coalesce(str_b, "+"),
        Sample = SAMPLE, Sampletype = "diagnosis",
        SVTYPE, driver_tier = tier, Discordant_readcount = dplyr::coalesce(DV, "")
      ) |>
      dplyr::arrange(Sample, chr_a, position_a)

    dir.create("protein_paint_out", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
    # Fixed descriptive name, matching the disco_plot_*/lollipop_* convention
    # used elsewhere in protein_paint_out/ (no PREFIX variable exists here).
    .out <- file.path("protein_paint_out", "sv_tier1_2.svfusion.txt")
    readr::write_tsv(pp_sv_fusion, .out, na = "")
    # fusioneditor expects `input` = the ENTIRE file as one string, "\n" line
    # breaks, tab-separated, header first. toJSON(auto_unbox) emits a correctly
    # escaped JS string literal.
    pp_sv_input_json <- as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(
      paste(readLines(.out, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), auto_unbox = TRUE))
    pp_sv_note <- sprintf("%d event(s) across %d sample(s) &rarr; <code>%s</code>",
                          nrow(pp_sv_fusion),
                          dplyr::n_distinct(pp_sv_fusion$Sample), .out)
  } else {
    pp_sv_note <- "No Tier 1/2 SVs with two breakpoints."
  }
} else {
  pp_sv_note <- "pass2_clean unavailable or missing required columns."
}
```

// Fusion Editor embed. Key names are case-sensitive; `input` (NOT `text`) is the
// documented parameter and takes the entire file content as one string.

## Row {.fill}

### Cohort recurrent SVs {title="Cohort recurrent SVs (Jasmine merge)"}

```{r cohort-merge-load}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

# ── COHORT_MERGE_SV results ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Populated only on PASS 2 of the two-pass render (see the header of
# modules/local/sv_report_index/main.nf). On pass 1 params$cohort_recurrent_tsv
# is "" and this section renders an explanatory card: pass 1's report is
# superseded by pass 2 whenever the merge runs, so an empty card there is
# expected, not a failure.
#
# The recurrence table is LONG -- one row per (cluster x sample). Two counts
# carry the interpretation (see modules/local/jasmine_cluster_map/main.nf):
#   n_tiered = samples where this SV was a Tier 1/2/3 call
#   n_any    = samples with ANY evidence in the cluster (Jasmine INFO/SUPP)
# n_tiered=1, n_any>=2 -> RESCUE candidate: called confidently in one sample and
#                         filtered out elsewhere despite supporting evidence.
# n_tiered=1, n_any=1  -> no corroboration; private call or false positive.
jm_recur    <- NULL
jm_note     <- NULL
jm_summary  <- NULL
jm_hdr_note <- NULL

# bgzf is gzip-readable, so the header can be pulled without an htslib dependency.
# Reads line-by-line and stops at the first non-"##" line rather than slurping a
# potentially large VCF body.
.read_vcf_header <- function(path, cap = 20000L) {
  con <- gzfile(path, "rt")
  on.exit(try(close(con), silent = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  out <- character(0)
  repeat {
    l <- readLines(con, n = 1L, warn = FALSE)
    if (length(l) == 0L || !startsWith(l, "##")) break
    out <- c(out, l)
    if (length(out) >= cap) break
  }
  out
}

.crt <- params$cohort_recurrent_tsv
if (is.character(.crt) && length(.crt) == 1L && nzchar(.crt) && file.exists(.crt)) {
  .tbl <- try(suppressWarnings(readr::read_tsv(
    .crt, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(.tbl, "try-error")) {
    jm_note <- sprintf("Could not read <code>%s</code>.", basename(.crt))
  } else if (nrow(.tbl) == 0) {
    jm_note <- paste0(
      "COHORT_MERGE_SV ran, but no cluster reached the recurrence threshold ",
      "(<code>cohort_sv_min_recurrence</code>). Expected on a two-sample test set.")
  } else {
    jm_recur <- .tbl
  }
} else {
  jm_note <- paste0(
    "Cohort SV merge results are not part of this render. Either this is ",
    "<b>pass 1</b> of the two-pass render &mdash; it produces the tiered table ",
    "that COHORT_MERGE_SV consumes, and pass 2 re-renders this page with the ",
    "merge results &mdash; or <code>run_cohort_merge_sv</code> is false.")
}

if (!is.null(jm_recur)) {
  .cols <- names(jm_recur)
  if (all(c("cluster_id", "n_tiered", "n_any") %in% .cols)) {
    jm_summary <- jm_recur |>
      dplyr::distinct(cluster_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
      dplyr::mutate(.nt = suppressWarnings(as.integer(n_tiered)),
                    .na = suppressWarnings(as.integer(n_any))) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        clusters              = dplyr::n(),
        `n_any >= 2`          = sum(.na >= 2, na.rm = TRUE),
        `n_tiered >= 2`       = sum(.nt >= 2, na.rm = TRUE),
        `rescue candidates`   = sum(.nt == 1 & .na >= 2, na.rm = TRUE))
    # Most-corroborated clusters first -- the rows a reviewer looks at.
    .ord <- intersect(c("cluster_id", "sample"), .cols)
    jm_recur <- jm_recur |>
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(suppressWarnings(as.integer(n_any))),
                     dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(.ord)))
  }
}

.cmv <- params$cohort_merged_vcf
if (is.character(.cmv) && length(.cmv) == 1L && nzchar(.cmv) && file.exists(.cmv)) {
  .hdr <- try(.read_vcf_header(.cmv), silent = TRUE)
  if (!inherits(.hdr, "try-error") && length(.hdr) > 0) {
    # Jasmine copies the header of its FIRST input, which here is a fully
    # VEP/AnnotSV-annotated per-sample VCF, so the upstream INFO definitions are
    # expected to survive the merge. Stated as a CHECK, not an assumption: the
    # card below reports which tags the merged file actually declares. Note that
    # a declared INFO tag is not the same as a populated one -- Jasmine emits one
    # representative record per cluster, so member-level annotations are taken
    # from the per-sample record table by JASMINE_CLUSTER_MAP, not from here.
    # NOT "CSQ": SPLIT_VEP_TO_INFO expands it into individual INFO fields
    # upstream, so CSQ is already absent from Jasmine's INPUT.
    .want <- c("Gene_name", "gnomAD_SV_AF", "ClinVar_SV_CLNSIG", "CALLER",
               "AnnotSV_ID", "ACMG_class", "AnnotSV_ranking_score",
               "SUPP_VEC", "SUPP", "IDLIST", "STARTVARIANCE")
    .have <- vapply(.want, function(k)
      any(grepl(sprintf("^##INFO=<ID=%s,", k), .hdr, perl = TRUE)), logical(1))
    jm_hdr_note <- sprintf(
      paste0("Merged VCF <code>%s</code> &mdash; %d header meta-lines. ",
             "INFO declared: <b>%s</b>. Absent: %s."),
      basename(.cmv), length(.hdr),
      if (any(.have))  paste(names(.have)[.have],  collapse = ", ") else "none",
      if (any(!.have)) paste(names(.have)[!.have], collapse = ", ") else "none")
  }
}
```

```{r cohort-merge-summary}
  knitr::kable(jm_summary, format = "html",
               table.attr = 'class="table table-sm" style="width:auto;"')
}
```

```{r cohort-merge-table}
    width      = "100%",
    extensions = c("Buttons", "Scroller"),

      scrollY = 420, scroller = TRUE, scrollX = TRUE, pageLength = 25
    ),
    caption = htmltools::tags$caption(

        "Jasmine cohort merge &mdash; one row per (cluster &times; sample). ",
        "<code>record_class</code> is TIERED when the row is in this report's ",
        "tiered table, and RESCUED when it is a sub-threshold call recovered ",
        "from the pre-filter VEP VCF. <code>n_tiered</code> against ",
        "<code>n_any</code> separates over-filtering from lack of ",
        "corroboration."))))
} else {
  htmltools::HTML(paste0("<p style='color:#666; margin:10px 0;'>", jm_note, "</p>"))
}
```

### SVTYPE {title="SVTYPE distribution"}

```{r plot-svtype}
#| eval: !expr nrow(pass2_long) > 0

p1 <- pass2_clean |>
  count(SAMPLE, SVTYPE, name = "n") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = SAMPLE, y = n, fill = SVTYPE,
             text = paste0("<b>Sample:</b> ", SAMPLE,
                           "<br><b>SVTYPE:</b> ", SVTYPE,
                           "<br><b>Variants (pass2):</b> ", n))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.9) +
  labs(title    = "Pass2 variants by SVTYPE",
       x = NULL, y = "Variant count") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))

ggplotly(p1, tooltip = "text") |> config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

### ACMG {title="ACMG class + AnnotSV ranking score"}

```{r plot-acmg}
#| eval: !expr nrow(pass2_long) > 0

p2a <- pass2_clean |>
  count(SAMPLE, ACMG_class_clean, name = "n") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = SAMPLE, y = n, fill = ACMG_class_clean,
             text = paste0("<b>Sample:</b> ", SAMPLE,
                           "<br><b>ACMG class:</b> ", ACMG_class_clean,
                           "<br><b>Variants:</b> ", n))) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = acmg_palette, name = "ACMG class",
                    drop = FALSE, na.value = "grey70") +
  labs(title    = "ACMG class distribution",
       subtitle = "counts of variants per sample, colored by ACMG ranking (NA = grey)",
       x = NULL, y = "Variant count") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))

# Plot the AnnotSV ranking score as jittered points (no violin / density).
# geom_violin crashes plotly's to_basic.GeomViolin when the layer's internal data frame
# has too few rows ("argument 1 is not a vector" from order(data[["y"]])).
# geom_jitter has no density step and works for any N ≥ 1.
p2b_data <- pass2_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(ranking_score), ranking_score > 0)

if (nrow(p2b_data) > 0) {
  p2b <- p2b_data |>
    ggplot(aes(x = SAMPLE, y = ranking_score, color = SAMPLE,
               text = paste0("<b>Sample:</b> ", SAMPLE,
                             "<br><b>ID:</b> ", ID,
                             "<br><b>SVTYPE:</b> ", SVTYPE,
                             "<br><b>AnnotSV ranking score:</b> ", ranking_score))) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, alpha = 0.8, size = 3) +
    scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.85, guide = "none") +
    labs(title    = "AnnotSV ranking score",
         subtitle = "Per-variant AnnotSV ranking score (jittered) — only records with score > 0 shown",
         x = NULL, y = "Score") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))

  subplot(ggplotly(p2a, tooltip = "text") |> config(displayModeBar = FALSE),
          ggplotly(p2b, tooltip = "text") |> config(displayModeBar = FALSE),
          nrows = 1, titleY = TRUE, margin = 0.06)
} else {
  ggplotly(p2a, tooltip = "text") |> config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
}
```
